metadata.title: Global Trading Strategy & Pine Script Glossary

TR-01.name: Donchian Channel Breakout
TR-01.alt_names: 唐奇安通道突破 · Прорыв канала Дончиана
TR-01.origin: Richard Donchian, US commodity research columns, late 1940s-1960s; popularized as the 4-week rule.
TR-01.core_idea: Buy when price closes above the highest high of the prior N bars and sell when it closes below the lowest low, letting the channel itself define trend participation. The channel doubles as the trailing exit on a shorter counter-channel. It is the direct ancestor of the Turtle system and of most later channel-breakout robots.
TR-01.rules: Enter long on close above the 20-bar (prior, offset by 1) high; exit on close below the 10-bar low; short mirrored.
TR-01.key_parameters: Entry channel 20 (55 for slow systems); exit channel 10 (20); works best on continuous futures and trending FX pairs.
TR-01.duplicates_eliminated: Turtle S1/S2; CN 海龟策略 templates (JoinQuant, myquant.cn); RU «Пробой канала» robots; vn.py TurtleSignalStrategy.
TR-01.pine_code:
//@version=5
strategy("Donchian 20-10 Breakout", overlay=true,
default_qty_type=strategy.percent_of_equity, default_qty_value=100)
nIn  = input.int(20, "Entry channel")
nOut = input.int(10, "Exit channel")
hi   = ta.highest(high, nIn)[1]
lo   = ta.lowest(low, nIn)[1]
xHi  = ta.highest(high, nOut)[1]
xLo  = ta.lowest(low, nOut)[1]
if strategy.position_size == 0 and close > hi
strategy.entry("L", strategy.long)
if strategy.position_size > 0 and close < xLo
strategy.close("L", comment="Exit channel")
if strategy.position_size == 0 and close < lo
strategy.entry("S", strategy.short)
if strategy.position_size < 0 and close > xHi
strategy.close("S", comment="Exit channel")
plot(hi, "Entry High", color=color.teal)
plot(lo, "Entry Low", color=color.red)

TR-02.name: Turtle Trading System (S1/S2)
TR-02.origin: Richard Dennis & William Eckhardt experiment, 1983-1988; full rules leaked online in 2003 and archived widely (Way of the Turtle, 2007).
TR-02.core_idea: A complete trend-following stack: Donchian entries (System 1 at 20 days, System 2 at 55 days), volatility-normalized unit sizing via ATR ('N'), 0.5N pyramiding up to 4 units, a 2N stop per unit, and channel exits. Its lasting contribution is sizing by volatility rather than conviction. Most later trend robots are Turtles with renamed parameters.
TR-02.rules: Unit = 1% of equity / ATR(20). Add a unit each +0.5N; stop the whole position at 2N from last fill; exit longs on a 10-day (S1) or 20-day (S2) low.
TR-02.key_parameters: N period 20; unit risk 1%; max 4 units; exits 10/20 days.
TR-02.duplicates_eliminated: 海龟交易法则 implementations on JoinQuant/BigQuant/vn.py (TurtleSignalStrategy); RU «Система Черепах» on Si/RTS futures; original Turtle Rules PDF archive.
TR-02.pine_code:
//@version=5
strategy("Turtle S2 Condensed (55/20, 2N stop)", overlay=true, pyramiding=4)
nLen    = input.int(20, "N length (ATR)")
riskPct = input.float(1.0, "Equity risk per unit, %", step=0.25)
N       = ta.atr(nLen)
entryHi = ta.highest(high, 55)[1]
exitLo  = ta.lowest(low, 20)[1]
var float lastFill = na
longSig = strategy.position_size == 0 and close > entryHi
addSig  = strategy.position_size > 0 and not na(lastFill) and close > lastFill + 0.5 * N and strategy.opentrades < 4
if longSig or addSig
strategy.entry("U" + str.tostring(strategy.opentrades + 1), strategy.long,
qty=(strategy.equity * riskPct / 100) / N)
lastFill := close
if strategy.position_size > 0 and ((not na(lastFill) and close < lastFill - 2 * N) or close < exitLo)
strategy.close_all(comment="2N stop or 20-day low")
lastFill := na

TR-03.name: Dual Moving Average Crossover (Golden Cross)
TR-03.alt_names: 双均线金叉死叉 · Пересечение скользящих средних
TR-03.origin: Attributed to Granville-era US practice; every retail platform ships it as the default example strategy.
TR-03.core_idea: Go long when a faster MA crosses above a slower MA and exit (or reverse) on the opposite cross. It is the 'Hello World' of quant trading — literally the default demo on JoinQuant — and remains a useful baseline to benchmark any trend model against. Its chronic weakness is whipsaw when the two averages are close in length.
TR-03.rules: Long on EMA(50) crossing above EMA(200) (or 5/20 on Chinese platforms); reverse or stop on the cross under; optional ATR trailing stop instead of reversal.
TR-03.key_parameters: Common pairs: 50/200 swing, 5/20 or 5/10 intraday; ATR stop 3x14.
TR-03.duplicates_eliminated: CN 双均线策略 (JoinQuant/myquant default demo, DoubleMaStrategy in vn.py); RU «Пересечение SMA 50/200»; MQL5 CodeBase MA-cross EAs.
TR-03.pine_code:
//@version=5
strategy("Dual MA Cross + ATR Stop", overlay=true)
fastLen = input.int(50, "Fast MA")
slowLen = input.int(200, "Slow MA")
atrMult = input.float(3.0, "Stop ATR multiple")
fast = ta.ema(close, fastLen)
slow = ta.ema(close, slowLen)
if ta.crossover(fast, slow)
strategy.entry("L", strategy.long)
if ta.crossunder(fast, slow)
strategy.entry("S", strategy.short)
if strategy.position_size > 0
strategy.exit("LX", from_entry="L", stop=close - atrMult * ta.atr(14))
if strategy.position_size < 0
strategy.exit("SX", from_entry="S", stop=close + atrMult * ta.atr(14))
plot(fast, "Fast EMA", color=color.teal)
plot(slow, "Slow EMA", color=color.orange)

TR-04.name: Granville Eight Rules of Moving Averages
TR-04.alt_names: 格兰维尔八大法则 · Восемь правил Гранвиля
TR-04.origin: Joseph Granville, 1960s US newsletters; formalized into scored strategies on JoinQuant (双均线-格兰维 strategy).
TR-04.core_idea: Rather than a single cross signal, Granville codified eight MA relationships: four buys (cross up, pullback to rising MA, break-then-reclaim, divergence away from a falling MA) and four sells (mirror). Chinese community strategies score all eight conditions into a 0-100 ranking and trade the highest-scoring names. It is an early example of signal confluence scoring now common in factor models.
TR-04.rules: Score MA alignment, price-vs-MA breakout, volume confirmation; buy top-ranked names when score exceeds threshold; sell on bearish rule triggers, fixed take-profit, or trailing stop from peak.
TR-04.key_parameters: Typical CN implementation: MA 5/10/20/60; volume ratio filter; 20% take-profit; 10% trailing stop.
TR-04.duplicates_eliminated: JoinQuant 双均线-格兰维交易 strategy; CN 移动平均线战法 variants; RU «Правила Гранвиля» tutorials (no separate robot).

TR-05.name: MACD Trend and Histogram System
TR-05.alt_names: MACD趋势+柱状图系统 · Система по MACD
TR-05.origin: Gerald Appel, 1970s (MACD); histogram by Thomas Aspray, 1986.
TR-05.core_idea: Trade the MACD line versus its signal line, filtered by the zero line so signals are only taken in the direction of the underlying momentum regime. The histogram's slope adds early warning of momentum loss before the actual cross. It remains one of the most-ported indicators on TradingView, MQL5, and Chinese platforms.
TR-05.rules: Long on MACD(12,26,9) crossing above signal while above zero; short mirrored; exit on opposite cross or histogram divergence.
TR-05.key_parameters: 12/26/9 standard; CN variants add 背离 (divergence) detection on the histogram.
TR-05.duplicates_eliminated: MACD+EMA combos in MQL5 CodeBase; CN MACD背离战法; vn.py MACD demo strategies.
TR-05.pine_code:
//@version=5
strategy("MACD Zero-Line Trend System", overlay=false)
[macdLine, sigLine, hist] = ta.macd(close, 12, 26, 9)
if ta.crossover(macdLine, sigLine) and macdLine > 0
strategy.entry("L", strategy.long)
if ta.crossunder(macdLine, sigLine) and macdLine < 0
strategy.entry("S", strategy.short)
plot(macdLine, "MACD", color=color.teal)
plot(sigLine, "Signal", color=color.orange)
plot(hist, "Histogram", style=plot.style_columns,
color=hist >= 0 ? color.new(color.teal, 40) : color.new(color.red, 40))
hline(0)

TR-06.name: Parabolic SAR Flip System
TR-06.alt_names: 抛物线SAR系统 · Система по Параболику SAR
TR-06.origin: J. Welles Wilder, New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems, 1978.
TR-06.core_idea: A perpetual-in-the-market stop-and-reverse system: dots trail price with an accelerating factor, and every stop hit flips the position. Wilder designed it for commodity trends; modern usage adds a filter (e.g., only long above a 200 EMA) because SAR bleeds badly in ranges. It survives everywhere as a trailing-stop visual.
TR-06.rules: Long while close is above SAR, flip short when close crosses below; acceleration 0.02 per new extreme, capped at 0.2.
TR-06.duplicates_eliminated: PSAR+EMA200+MACD signal packs (multiple GitHub repos); CN SAR跟踪策略; RU «Параболик» robots.
TR-06.pine_code:
//@version=5
strategy("Parabolic SAR Flip", overlay=true)
start = input.float(0.02, "Start")
inc   = input.float(0.02, "Increment")
maxv  = input.float(0.2, "Max")
sar = ta.sar(start, inc, maxv)
if close > sar and strategy.position_size <= 0
strategy.entry("L", strategy.long)
if close < sar and strategy.position_size >= 0
strategy.entry("S", strategy.short)
plot(sar, "SAR", style=plot.style_circles,
color=strategy.position_size >= 0 ? color.teal : color.red)

TR-07.name: ADX/DMI Trend Filter System
TR-07.alt_names: ADX/DMI趋势过滤系统 · Система на ADX/DMI
TR-07.origin: J. Welles Wilder, 1978; refined by numerous TASC articles.
TR-07.core_idea: Use +DI/-DI crossovers for direction and ADX as a regime gate: only take DI signals while ADX is rising above ~20-25, which separates trending from chopping conditions. As a standalone it underperforms its filters' reputation, but as an overlay it is attached to half of the breakout systems in this glossary. Chinese CTA templates and Smart-Lab robots both use it almost identically.
TR-07.rules: Long when +DI crosses above -DI with ADX > 20 and rising; exit on reverse cross or ADX rolling over from a high.
TR-07.key_parameters: DMI 14; ADX threshold 20-25; optional exit at ADX peak.
TR-07.duplicates_eliminated: ADX gates inside CN CTA templates (文华/TB); RU «ADX-фильтр» modules; generic MT4 ADX EAs.

TR-08.name: SuperTrend
TR-08.origin: Olivier Seban (France), circa 2009; hundreds of open Pine ports.
TR-08.core_idea: An ATR band flipped around price: the level trails beneath uptrends and above downtrends by factor x ATR, and crossing it flips the position. It is conceptually Wilder's vol-stop with a cleaner flip mechanic, which is why it replaced SAR in most modern retail systems. Its exposure is near-binary, so it is usually paired with a higher-timeframe filter.
TR-08.rules: Long while price is above the SuperTrend line (direction -1), short while below; flips on close through the line.
TR-08.key_parameters: Factor 3, ATR 10 (classic); factor 2-4, ATR 7-14 in the wild.
TR-08.duplicates_eliminated: CN 超级趋势 (JoinQuant/文华); RU «Супертренд» TradingView scripts; countless 'ST + filter' hybrids on MQL5.
TR-08.pine_code:
//@version=5
strategy("SuperTrend Flip", overlay=true)
factor = input.float(3.0, "Factor")
atrLen = input.int(10, "ATR Length")
[st, dir] = ta.supertrend(factor, atrLen)
if dir < 0
strategy.entry("L", strategy.long)
if dir > 0
strategy.entry("S", strategy.short)
plot(dir < 0 ? st : na, "ST Up", color=color.teal, style=plot.style_linebr)
plot(dir > 0 ? st : na, "ST Down", color=color.red, style=plot.style_linebr)

TR-09.name: UT Bot Alerts (ATR Trailing Stop on Close)
TR-09.origin: Yo_adriiiiaan on TradingView (2020), popularized by QuantNomad videos; ATR trailing-stop lineage from 2010s forex forums.
TR-09.core_idea: A recursive ATR trailing stop computed on closes: the stop only ratchets in the trend direction and flips when close crosses it, producing sparse buy/sell alerts. Its popularity comes from clean visualization and alert-driven automation rather than novelty — it is mathematically inside the SuperTrend/Chandelier family. Widely cloned with EMA, HTF, or session filters bolted on.
TR-09.rules: Trail = close -/+ key x ATR(period), ratcheting only; long when close crosses above the down-trail, exit/short on cross under the up-trail.
TR-09.key_parameters: Key (sensitivity) 2 (1-3 typical); ATR period 10 (or 1 in aggressive clones).
TR-09.duplicates_eliminated: Original 'ATR Trailing Stops' scripts (R	thomson bands, 2018); RU 'Универсальный трейлинг' packs; UT Bot + EMA 200 variants (QuantNomad).
TR-09.pine_code:
//@version=5
strategy("UT Bot-Style ATR Trailing Stop", overlay=true)
keyA   = input.float(2.0, "Sensitivity")
atrLen = input.int(10, "ATR Length")
nLoss  = keyA * ta.atr(atrLen)
var float up = na
var float dn = na
up := close > nz(up[1], close) and close[1] > nz(up[1], close) ?
math.max(nz(up[1]), close - nLoss) : close - nLoss
dn := close < nz(dn[1], close) and close[1] < nz(dn[1], close) ?
math.min(nz(dn[1]), close + nLoss) : close + nLoss
if ta.crossover(close, dn)
strategy.entry("L", strategy.long)
if ta.crossunder(close, up)
strategy.entry("S", strategy.short)
plot(ta.crossover(close, dn) ? dn : na, "Buy", style=plot.style_circles, color=color.teal, linewidth=3)
plot(ta.crossunder(close, up) ? up : na, "Sell", style=plot.style_circles, color=color.red, linewidth=3)

TR-10.name: Chandelier Exit
TR-10.origin: Chuck LeBeau, 1990s (Systems & Exchanges seminars; popularized via TASC).
TR-10.core_idea: Trail a stop at the highest high since entry minus a multiple of ATR, hanging from the 'chandelier' rather than from entry price. As a standalone system it rides trends with a volatility-scaled ratchet and re-enters when the trend state flips. It is the professional-grade ancestor of most modern trailing-stop scripts including UT Bot and SuperTrend variants.
TR-10.rules: Long stop = highest high(22) - 3 x ATR(22); flip trend when the stop is breached; short mirrored.
TR-10.duplicates_eliminated: ATR Trailing Stops (Wilders-based); 'QQE trailing' variants; CN 吊灯止损 modules in CTA templates.
TR-10.pine_code:
//@version=5
strategy("Chandelier Exit Trend Rider", overlay=true)
nLen = input.int(22, "Lookback")
mult = input.float(3.0, "ATR Multiple")
longStop  = ta.highest(high, nLen) - mult * ta.atr(nLen)
shortStop = ta.lowest(low, nLen) + mult * ta.atr(nLen)
var float trail = na
var int   trend = 1
trend := close > nz(trail[1], shortStop) ? 1 :
close < nz(trail[1], longStop) ? -1 : nz(trend[1], 1)
trail := trend == 1 ? math.max(longStop, nz(trail[1], longStop)) :
math.min(shortStop, nz(trail[1], shortStop))
if trend == 1 and nz(trend[1]) == -1
strategy.entry("L", strategy.long)
if trend == -1 and nz(trend[1]) == 1
strategy.entry("S", strategy.short)
plot(trend == 1 ? trail : na, "Long trail", color=color.teal, style=plot.style_linebr)
plot(trend == -1 ? trail : na, "Short trail", color=color.red, style=plot.style_linebr)

TR-11.name: Ichimoku Kinko Hyo
TR-11.alt_names: 一目均衡表 · 一目均衡表 (Ишимоку)
TR-11.core_idea: A five-part system — conversion and base lines (Donchian-style midpoints), a leading span computed from them, a 52-period span, and a displaced cloud — that encodes trend, momentum, support/resistance, and forward projection in one overlay. Trading rules combine cloud position, Kijun as the trend referee, and TK crosses. It has dedicated practitioner schools in Japan, China (一目均衡表 communities), and Russia, where 'Ишимоку' became a retail cult in the 2000s.
TR-11.rules: Long when price is above the cloud, Tenkan > Kijun, and Chikou is clear of price; Kijun bounces or TK crosses with cloud alignment trigger entries; exit on TK cross against or Kijun break.
TR-11.duplicates_eliminated: CN 一目均衡表 strategy packs; RU Ишимоку school variants (see RU-10); MT4 Ichimoku EAs.
TR-11.pine_code:
//@version=5
strategy("Ichimoku Kinko Hyo", overlay=true)
donchian(len) => math.avg(ta.highest(high, len), ta.lowest(low, len))
tenkan = donchian(9)
kijun  = donchian(26)
spanA  = math.avg(tenkan, kijun)
spanB  = donchian(52)
cloudHi = math.max(spanA[26], spanB[26])
cloudLo = math.min(spanA[26], spanB[26])
longCond  = close > kijun and close > cloudHi and tenkan > kijun
shortCond = close < kijun and close < cloudLo and tenkan < kijun
if longCond
strategy.entry("L", strategy.long)
if shortCond
strategy.entry("S", strategy.short)
plot(tenkan, "Tenkan", color=color.teal)
plot(kijun, "Kijun", color=color.red)
plot(spanA, "Span A", color=color.new(color.teal, 60), offset=26)
plot(spanB, "Span B", color=color.new(color.red, 60), offset=26)

TR-12.name: Kaufman Adaptive Moving Average (KAMA)
TR-12.alt_names: 卡玛自适应均线 · Адаптивная средняя Кауфмана
TR-12.core_idea: KAMA scales its own smoothing constant by an Efficiency Ratio: when price travels cleanly (high ER) it hugs price like a fast EMA, and in noise (low ER) it flattens like a long SMA. This makes it a single-line trend filter that self-throttles in ranges. Traders either trade close-vs-KAMA crosses or use KAMA slope as the regime gate for other entries.
TR-12.rules: Long on close crossing above KAMA with rising slope; exit on cross under or slope flattening; short mirrored.
TR-12.key_parameters: Window 10, fast 2, slow 30 (canonical); CN CTA uses 10/2/30 on commodity futures.
TR-12.duplicates_eliminated: KAMA modules in CN CTA kits (文华/TB); RU «АМА Кауфмана» robots; KAMA+filter packs on MQL5.
TR-12.pine_code:
//@version=5
strategy("Kaufman Adaptive MA Trend", overlay=true)
len   = input.int(10, "Efficiency window")
fastE = input.int(2, "Fast smoothing")
slowE = input.int(30, "Slow smoothing")
chg = math.abs(close - close[len])
vol = math.sum(math.abs(ta.change(close)), len)
er  = chg / math.max(vol, syminfo.mintick)
sc  = math.pow(er * (2.0 / (fastE + 1) - 2.0 / (slowE + 1)) + 2.0 / (slowE + 1), 2)
var float kama = na
kama := na(kama[1]) ? close : kama[1] + sc * (close - kama[1])
if ta.crossover(close, kama)
strategy.entry("L", strategy.long)
if ta.crossunder(close, kama)
strategy.entry("S", strategy.short)
plot(kama, "KAMA", color=color.teal)

TR-13.name: VIDYA (Variable Index Dynamic Average)
TR-13.origin: Tushar Chande, 1992 (Technical Analysis of Stocks & Commodities).
TR-13.core_idea: VIDYA multiplies the EMA increment by the absolute momentum of a CMO, so the average speeds up in directional markets and stalls in noise — an alternative adaptive-MA solution to KAMA with different lag structure. It is usually used as the trend line inside breakout or pullback systems rather than as a cross system itself.
TR-13.rules: Treat VIDYA like an adaptive EMA in a dual-MA or pullback system; slope direction acts as the regime filter.
TR-13.key_parameters: Length 9-20 with CMO(9) scaling is typical.
TR-13.duplicates_eliminated: VIDYA in MetaStock/AmiBroker libraries (the 1990s archive era); MT4 VIDYA indicators; RU VIDYA forks.

TR-14.name: FRAMA (Fractal Adaptive Moving Average)
TR-14.origin: John Ehlers, 2005 (TASC; fractal dimension work with Ric Way).
TR-14.core_idea: FRAMA computes a fractal dimension from half-window high/low geometry and maps it into an adaptive exponential weighting: smooth trends drive dimension toward 1 (fast MA), choppy ranges toward 2 (very slow MA). It is the most theoretically grounded of the adaptive-MA trio (KAMA, VIDYA, FRAMA) and behaves best on swing timeframes.
TR-14.rules: Use as a single-line trend filter; trade price-vs-FRAMA crosses with slope confirmation, or gate other systems with FRAMA slope.
TR-14.key_parameters: Base length 16 (windows of len/2); alpha clamped [0.01, 1.0].
TR-14.duplicates_eliminated: FRAMA ports in TASC Traders' Tips archive; MT4/MT5 FRAMA; CN 分形均线 experiments.

TR-15.name: Guppy Multiple Moving Averages (GMMA)
TR-15.alt_names: 顾比复合移动平均线 · GMMA Ганна Гаппи
TR-15.origin: Daryl Guppy (Australia), Trading Tactics, 1990s; huge uptake in Chinese retail materials (顾比均线).
TR-15.core_idea: Twelve EMAs (3-15 and 30-60) split into a short-term 'traders' group and long-term 'investors' group; the geometry between the groups — compression, expansion, and crossover of the ribbons — reads consensus and disagreement. Trades are taken on group compression followed by expansion in the trend direction. It is a ribbon visualization of trend stability rather than a mechanical signal, which is why most implementations remain indicator-only.
TR-15.rules: Long when the fast ribbon crosses above and the slow ribbon expands with both sloping up; exit when ribbons compress and interpenetrate.
TR-15.duplicates_eliminated: CN 顾比均线 templates (通达信/同花顺 formulas); RU «Вееры Ганна/Гаппи» ribbon packs.
TR-15.pine_code:
//@version=5
indicator("Guppy Multiple Moving Averages (GMMA)", overlay=true)
plot(ta.ema(close, 3),  "F3",  color=color.new(color.teal, 0))
plot(ta.ema(close, 5),  "F5",  color=color.new(color.teal, 20))
plot(ta.ema(close, 8),  "F8",  color=color.new(color.teal, 30))
plot(ta.ema(close, 10), "F10", color=color.new(color.teal, 40))
plot(ta.ema(close, 12), "F12", color=color.new(color.teal, 50))
plot(ta.ema(close, 15), "F15", color=color.new(color.teal, 60))
plot(ta.ema(close, 30), "S30", color=color.new(color.red, 0))
plot(ta.ema(close, 35), "S35", color=color.new(color.red, 20))
plot(ta.ema(close, 40), "S40", color=color.new(color.red, 30))
plot(ta.ema(close, 45), "S45", color=color.new(color.red, 40))
plot(ta.ema(close, 50), "S50", color=color.new(color.red, 50))
plot(ta.ema(close, 60), "S60", color=color.new(color.red, 60))

TR-16.name: Heikin-Ashi Trend Flip
TR-16.alt_names: 平均K线趋势翻转 · Торговля по Хейкин-Аши
TR-16.origin: Munehisa Homma's candle lineage; Heikin-Ashi formalized for modern charts by Dan Valcu (2004, 'Using Heikin-Ashi technique').
TR-16.core_idea: Heikin-Ashi averages open/close into pseudo-candles whose bodies shrink in chop and stretch in trends; a run of same-color HA candles with full bodies is a high-contrast trend state. Systems flip long/short after N consecutive colored bodies with a minimum body size, or simply exit on the first opposite-colored candle. It is best treated as a regime filter because HA values are recursive and repaint the 'real' OHLC.
TR-16.rules: Long after 2 consecutive up HA bodies of at least 0.5 ATR; flip/exit on the mirror condition.
TR-16.key_parameters: Run length 2-3; body filter 0.5 x ATR(14).
TR-16.duplicates_eliminated: HA smoothing packs (every platform); CN Heikin-Ashi策略; RU «Хейкин Аши» scalping variants.
TR-16.pine_code:
//@version=5
strategy("Heikin-Ashi Trend Flip", overlay=true)
nRun = input.int(2, "Consecutive HA bars")
atrF = input.float(0.5, "Min body as ATR fraction")
var float haO = na
var float haC = na
haO := na(haO[1]) ? (open + close) / 2 : (haO[1] + haC[1]) / 2
haC := (open + high + low + close) / 4
body  = haC - haO
upRun = nz(ta.barssince(body <= 0), 999)
dnRun = nz(ta.barssince(body >= 0), 999)
bigEnough = math.abs(body) > atrF * ta.atr(14)
if upRun == nRun and bigEnough and strategy.position_size <= 0
strategy.entry("L", strategy.long)
if dnRun == nRun and bigEnough and strategy.position_size >= 0
strategy.entry("S", strategy.short)

TR-17.name: Time-Series Momentum (TSMOM)
TR-17.alt_names: 时间序列动量 · Моментум по времени
TR-17.origin: Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen, Journal of Financial Economics, 2012 (AQR lineage).
TR-17.core_idea: Go long an asset if its own return over the past k months (commonly 12) is positive, short if negative, sized inversely to volatility. The paper documented that this simple sign rule monetizes the autocorrelation institutional CTAs create, across 58 instruments over decades. It is the academic formalization of what Donchian/Turtle systems do mechanically, and the backbone of most CTA replication products.
TR-17.rules: Sign of trailing 12-month return decides direction; position = target vol / realized vol; rebalance monthly.
TR-17.duplicates_eliminated: Cross-sectional momentum (ST-04); CTA trend replication funds; CN 商品CTA趋势 replication research.

TR-18.name: CANSLIM Momentum / Leading-Stock Playbook
TR-18.origin: William O'Neil, How to Make Money in Stocks (1988; Investor's Business Daily methodology).
TR-18.core_idea: A fundamentals-plus-technique momentum system: buy stocks meeting Current earnings, Annual growth, New product/price highs, Supply/demand, Leaders, Institutional sponsorship, and Market direction, entered chiefly on cup-with-handle or flat-base breakouts in strong uptrends. Exits are hard rules: cut at 7-8% below entry, take profits into climactic runs. It is the direct ancestor of Qullamägi-style EP momentum (see BK-03 relatives) and of A-share 龙头战法 (CN-04) logic.
TR-18.rules: Screen by earnings/price leadership; buy base breakouts above pivot with volume surge; stop 7-8%; pyramiding only while the advance stays orderly.
TR-18.key_parameters: Relative strength top percentile; volume >= 1.5x average on breakout; bases 3-7 weeks.
TR-18.duplicates_eliminated: IBD-style screeners; CN 龙头战法 (structurally similar); RU «рост на лидерах» screeners.

MR-01.name: Connors RSI(2) Pullback
MR-01.alt_names: 康纳斯RSI(2)回调 · Система RSI(2) Коннорса
MR-01.origin: Laurence Connors, Short Term Trading Strategies That Work (2009) and Connors Research papers.
MR-01.core_idea: Buy short-term panic inside an uptrend: RSI(2) under 10 while price is above its 200-day average, exit into the snap-back near RSI 55-65 or the 5-day MA. The edge is heavily documented on US equities and ETFs and degrades on assets with fat left tails. It is the archetype of 'buy the dip, sell the rip' mechanical scalping.
MR-01.rules: Long when trend filter true and RSI(2) < buy level; exit when RSI(2) > exit level or close > SMA(5); short mirror below the 200-day MA.
MR-01.key_parameters: RSI 2 (3-5 variants); buy <10, exit >60; 200-MA regime filter.
MR-01.duplicates_eliminated: RSI(3)/RSI(4) variants; CN 短线超卖反弹 templates; RU 'RSI отскок' MT4 robots.
MR-01.pine_code:
//@version=5
strategy("RSI(2) Pullback (Connors-style)", overlay=true)
rsiLen = input.int(2, "RSI length")
buyLv  = input.int(10, "Buy below")
sellLv = input.int(60, "Exit above")
trendOk = close > ta.sma(close, 200)
r = ta.rsi(close, rsiLen)
if trendOk and r < buyLv
strategy.entry("L", strategy.long)
if strategy.position_size > 0 and (r > sellLv or close > ta.sma(close, 5))
strategy.close("L", comment="Snap-back exit")

MR-02.name: Bollinger Band Reversion (%B Fade)
MR-02.alt_names: 布林带回归 · Отскок от границ Боллинджера
MR-02.core_idea: Price outside a 2-sigma band is statistically stretched; fade back to the mean basis, ideally only in the direction of the higher-timeframe trend. Bollinger himself warns that walking the band is a trend signal, so serious implementations add a trend gate or a squeeze precondition. It is one of the two or three most universal retail strategies on earth.
MR-02.rules: Long when trend-up and close pierces the lower band, exit at the middle band; short mirrored; optional RSI confluence.
MR-02.key_parameters: Length 20, deviations 2.0; exit at SMA(20); RSI(14) < 30 confluence.
MR-02.duplicates_eliminated: CN 布林带下轨抄底 (ETF/股票); RU «торговля от границ Боллинджера»; Bollinger %B factor research.
MR-02.pine_code:
//@version=5
strategy("Bollinger Band Reversion", overlay=true)
len  = input.int(20, "Length")
mult = input.float(2.0, "StdDev")
basis = ta.sma(close, len)
dev   = mult * ta.stdev(close, len)
lower = basis - dev
trendUp = close > ta.sma(close, 200)
if trendUp and close < lower
strategy.entry("L", strategy.long)
if strategy.position_size > 0 and close >= basis
strategy.close("L", comment="Mean reversion")

MR-03.name: Double 7s / 3-Day High-Low Pullback
MR-03.origin: Laurence Connors & Cesar Alvarez, Connors Research (2010s).
MR-03.core_idea: An extremely simple pullback quantification: buy when close is at its lowest of the last 7 days but the market is above its 200-day MA, exit at the highest close of the last 7 days. Variants substitute 3-day windows or add a cumulative RS filter. It demonstrates how small the mean-reversion edge can be while still being systematic.
MR-03.rules: Long on 7-day-low close above SMA(200); exit on 7-day-high close; time-stop optional.
MR-03.key_parameters: Window 7 (3-day variant); 200-MA filter; position ~equally weighted across a basket.
MR-03.duplicates_eliminated: 3-Day High/Low; 'TFSE' Connors variants; CN 七日新低反弹 scripts.

MR-04.name: Keltner Channel Pullback
MR-04.alt_names: 肯特纳通道回调 · Откат по каналам Кельтнера
MR-04.origin: Chester Keltner, 1960 (10-day MA of typical price); modern ATR version by Linda Raschke, 1990s.
MR-04.core_idea: Raschke's modernization sets the channel at EMA(20) +/- 1.5-2 x ATR(10); mean-reversion traders fade the outer band back to the EMA, while trend traders use the opposite (KingKeltner breakout in vn.py). The same envelope therefore hosts two opposite philosophies depending on whether the trend filter is inside or outside the system. This entry covers the fade form; the breakout form is BK-13.
MR-04.rules: Long when close < lower Keltner band in an uptrend regime; exit at the EMA basis or opposite band.
MR-04.duplicates_eliminated: vn.py KingKeltnerStrategy (breakout form, cross-ref BK-13); CN 肯特纳通道 scripts; RU каналы Кельтнера.

MR-05.name: TTM Squeeze / Squeeze Momentum
MR-05.alt_names: 布林-KC挤压 · Сжатие Боллинджера и Кельтнера
MR-05.origin: John Carter, Mastering the Trade (2005); LazyBear's open Pine port (2014) made it a TradingView staple.
MR-05.core_idea: When Bollinger Bands fit entirely inside Keltner Channels, volatility has compressed to a coiled state; the script fires when the squeeze releases, in the direction of a linreg momentum histogram measured against the midpoint of the range. It is a volatility-contraction breakout disguised as an oscillator and is among the most-cloned scripts on TradingView.
MR-05.rules: Arm during squeeze-on; enter on squeeze fire with histogram positive (long) or negative (short); trail via histogram color flips or ATR stop.
MR-05.duplicates_eliminated: Squeeze Momentum Indicator [LazyBear]; Squeeze Pro (LuxAlgo, cross-ref BK-11); CN 布林收口战法; RU «сжатие волатильности» scripts.
MR-05.pine_code:
//@version=5
strategy("TTM Squeeze", overlay=false)
lenBB = input.int(20, "BB length")
multBB = input.float(2.0, "BB mult")
lenKC = input.int(20, "KC length")
multKC = input.float(1.5, "KC mult")
basis = ta.sma(close, lenBB)
dev   = multBB * ta.stdev(close, lenBB)
bbU   = basis + dev
bbL   = basis - dev
ma    = ta.ema(close, lenKC)
rng   = ta.atr(lenKC)
kcU   = ma + multKC * rng
kcL   = ma - multKC * rng
squeezeOn = bbU < kcU and bbL > kcL
mom = ta.linreg(close - math.avg(math.avg(ta.highest(high, lenKC),
ta.lowest(low, lenKC)), ta.sma(close, lenKC)), lenKC, 0)
fired = squeezeOn[1] and not squeezeOn
if fired and mom > 0
strategy.entry("L", strategy.long)
if fired and mom < 0
strategy.entry("S", strategy.short)
plot(mom, "Momentum", style=plot.style_histogram,
color=mom >= 0 ? color.teal : color.red)
hline(0)
bgcolor(squeezeOn ? color.new(color.orange, 80) : na)

MR-06.name: QQE (Qualitative Quantitative Estimation)
MR-06.origin: MT4 forex community (2000s); famous 'QQE mod' by Glaz on TradingView (2014+); MT4 port by Mihkel00.
MR-06.core_idea: QQE smooths RSI with a short EMA and wraps it in a Wilder-style ATR-of-the-RSI trailing band, so signals are RSI crosses of a volatility-adjusted trail rather than raw oversold touches. The construction gives RSI trend-following behavior with far fewer whipsaws. It is beloved in forex and gold scalping communities in both Russian and Chinese forums.
MR-06.rules: Long when the smoothed RSI crosses above its lower ATR trail; short on the cross under the upper trail; optional 50-line regime filter.
MR-06.key_parameters: RSI 14, smoothing 5, Wilder 14, factor 4.238 (classic mod settings).
MR-06.duplicates_eliminated: QQE MOD (Glaz, Mihkel00 ports); RU QQE-форекс советники; CN QQE+MACD hybrids.
MR-06.pine_code:
//@version=5
strategy("QQE (RSI + RSI-ATR Trailing)", overlay=false)
rsiLen  = input.int(14, "RSI length")
smLen   = input.int(5, "RSI smoothing")
wildLen = input.int(14, "Wilder length")
sf      = input.float(4.238, "ATR factor")
rsi   = ta.rsi(close, rsiLen)
rsiMa = ta.ema(rsi, smLen)
dar   = ta.ema(ta.rma(math.abs(rsiMa - nz(rsiMa[1], rsiMa)), wildLen), 2 * wildLen - 1)
band  = sf * dar
var float trailUp = na
var float trailDn = na
trailUp := nz(rsiMa[1], rsiMa) > nz(trailUp[1], 0) and rsiMa > nz(trailUp[1], 0) ?
math.max(nz(trailUp[1]), rsiMa - band) : rsiMa - band
trailDn := nz(rsiMa[1], rsiMa) < nz(trailDn[1], 100) and rsiMa < nz(trailDn[1], 100) ?
math.min(nz(trailDn[1]), rsiMa + band) : rsiMa + band
if ta.crossover(rsiMa, trailDn)
strategy.entry("L", strategy.long)
if ta.crossunder(rsiMa, trailUp)
strategy.entry("S", strategy.short)
plot(rsiMa, "RSI MA", color=color.teal)
plot(trailUp, "Fast trail", color=color.new(color.red, 30))
plot(trailDn, "Slow trail", color=color.new(color.teal, 30))
hline(50)

MR-07.name: WaveTrend Oscillator
MR-07.alt_names: 波形震荡器 · Волновой осциллятор WaveTrend
MR-07.origin: Ported from TradeStation/MetaTrader origins by LazyBear (2014) — 'The Perfectionist' lineage; exact original author unknown.
MR-07.core_idea: WaveTrend measures the typical price's distance from its own EMA, normalized by 0.015 x an EMA of absolute deviation, then double-smoothed — producing a very smooth cycle oscillator with distinctive overbought/oversold plateaus. Trades fire on WT1/WT2 crosses at extremes. It is one of the top-installed community oscillators ever and the standard confirmation layer in crypto scalping dashboards.
MR-07.rules: Long on WT1 crossing above WT2 below the oversold band; short on the cross under above overbought; exit near the zero line.
MR-07.key_parameters: Channel length 10, average 21, bands +/-53; signal SMA 4.
MR-07.duplicates_eliminated: WaveTrend [WT] (LazyBear); SJ WaveTrend and dozens of forks; CN WT+VWAP scalping dashboards; RU WaveTrend forks on MQL5.
MR-07.pine_code:
//@version=5
strategy("WaveTrend Oscillator Cross", overlay=false)
chLen  = input.int(10, "Channel length")
avgLen = input.int(21, "Average length")
obLv   = input.float(53, "Overbought")
osLv   = input.float(-53, "Oversold")
ap  = hlc3
esa = ta.ema(ap, chLen)
d   = ta.ema(math.abs(ap - esa), chLen)
ci  = (ap - esa) / (0.015 * math.max(d, syminfo.mintick))
wt1 = ta.ema(ci, avgLen)
wt2 = ta.sma(wt1, 4)
if ta.crossover(wt1, wt2) and wt1 < osLv
strategy.entry("L", strategy.long)
if ta.crossunder(wt1, wt2) and wt1 > obLv
strategy.entry("S", strategy.short)
plot(wt1, "WT1", color=color.teal)
plot(wt2, "WT2", color=color.red)
hline(obLv)
hline(osLv)
hline(0)

MR-08.name: Fisher Transform Reversal
MR-08.alt_names: 费雪变换反转 · Преобразование Фишера
MR-08.origin: John Ehlers, 'Using the Fisher Transform', TASC November 2002.
MR-08.core_idea: The Fisher transform maps any bounded oscillator (here a normalized price position in its range) through a logit-like function that sharpens turning points: ordinary swings become nearly Gaussian-peaked, so crossings of the transformed line with its 1-bar lag mark reversals unusually cleanly. Ehlers designed it to make cycle turning points unambiguous for mechanical exits.
MR-08.rules: Long on Fisher crossing above its previous value while negative; short on the cross under while positive; exit on opposite signal or zero-line pass.
MR-08.key_parameters: Length 9; clamps the normalized value to +/-0.999.
MR-08.duplicates_eliminated: Fisher in Ehlers' book suite (Cybernetic Analysis, 2002); MT4/MT5 Fisher; CN 费雪指标 scripts.
MR-08.pine_code:
//@version=5
strategy("Ehlers Fisher Transform", overlay=false)
len = input.int(9, "Length")
hh  = ta.highest(high, len)
ll  = ta.lowest(low, len)
rng = math.max(hh - ll, syminfo.mintick)
var float val = 0.0
var float fish = 0.0
val  := 0.33 * 2.0 * ((close - ll) / rng - 0.5) + 0.67 * nz(val[1])
val  := math.max(math.min(val, 0.999), -0.999)
fish := 0.5 * math.log((1 + val) / (1 - val)) + 0.5 * nz(fish[1])
if ta.crossover(fish, nz(fish[1])) and fish < 0
strategy.entry("L", strategy.long)
if ta.crossunder(fish, nz(fish[1])) and fish > 0
strategy.entry("S", strategy.short)
plot(fish, "Fisher", color=color.teal)
plot(nz(fish[1]), "Trigger", color=color.red)
hline(0)

MR-09.name: RSI Regular Divergence System
MR-09.alt_names: RSI背离系统 · Дивергенции по RSI
MR-09.origin: Classic manual TA (Wilder's RSI, 1978) mechanized via pivot detection in the Pine community (2010s).
MR-09.core_idea: A regular bullish divergence forms when price prints a lower low while RSI prints a higher low — selling exhaustion. Mechanical detection compares the last two RSI pivot lows and the price lows between them, then enters on confirmation. Divergence systems look brilliant on annotated screenshots and are much noisier in backtests, so implementations always add trend and volatility filters.
MR-09.rules: Detect RSI pivot lows (5/5); long when a new lower price low pairs with a higher RSI low, above a 200-MA; exit on RSI failing above 70.
MR-09.key_parameters: Pivot left/right 5; RSI 14; divergence lookback ~60 bars.
MR-09.duplicates_eliminated: Hidden divergence variants; CN MACD/RSI背离战法; RU 'дивергенция' robots on MQL5.
MR-09.pine_code:
//@version=5
strategy("RSI Regular Divergence", overlay=false)
rsiLen = input.int(14, "RSI")
lbL = input.int(5, "Pivot left")
lbR = input.int(5, "Pivot right")
rsi = ta.rsi(close, rsiLen)
pl  = ta.pivotlow(rsi, lbL, lbR)
var float lastPL = na
var float prevPL = na
var float lastPLPrice = na
var float prevPLPrice = na
if not na(pl)
prevPL      := lastPL
prevPLPrice := lastPLPrice
lastPL      := pl
lastPLPrice := low[lbR]
bullDiv = not na(prevPL) and lastPL > prevPL and lastPLPrice < prevPLPrice
if bullDiv and close > ta.sma(close, 200)
strategy.entry("L", strategy.long)
if strategy.position_size > 0 and ta.crossunder(rsi, 70)
strategy.close("L", comment="RSI roll")
plot(rsi, "RSI", color=color.teal)
hline(30)
hline(70)

MR-10.name: Stochastic Oversold System
MR-10.alt_names: 随机指标超卖系统 · Система по стохастику
MR-10.core_idea: Fade %K/%D extremes toward the middle of the range, classically demanding a cross out of the 20/80 zones as confirmation rather than entry at the extreme itself. Lane's original framing tied the indicator to cycle troughs; modern use adds trend filters because raw stochastic fades bleed in trends. It remains the default oscillator in Russian and Chinese retail platforms.
MR-10.rules: Long when %K crosses above %D from below 20; exit at 50 or 80; short mirrored.
MR-10.duplicates_eliminated: RU «Стохастик + RSI» комбо-роботы; CN KDJ战法 (the CN KDJ is a stochastic variant); MT4 stochastic packs.

MR-11.name: Pivot Point Reversion
MR-11.alt_names: 枢轴点回归 · Торговля от пивотов
MR-11.origin: Floor-trader pivots, pre-digital Chicago pits; codified in 1990s day-trading literature (Crabel, Pesavento).
MR-11.core_idea: Compute R1/S1 pivots from the prior session's high/low/close and fade touches back toward the central pivot when the day is range-bound. The system is a session-anchored mean reversion with unusually clean institutional logic — everyone watches the same levels. It requires an intraday trend filter (e.g., yesterday's close vs today's open) to avoid fading real trend days.
MR-11.rules: Long at S1 if open > prior close (gap-up bias); exit at PP or R1; short mirrored; skip on wide-gap trend days.
MR-11.key_parameters: Classic pivot formulas; skip threshold for gaps > 0.5 x ATR.
MR-11.duplicates_eliminated: CN 分时均线/枢轴 strategies; RU 'пивот-уровни' robots; every MT4 pivot indicator pack.

MR-12.name: Intraday VWAP Mean Reversion
MR-12.alt_names: VWAP日内均值回归 · Возврат к VWAP
MR-12.origin: Institutional execution benchmark turned retail signal (1990s-2000s); Pine ta.vwap session form.
MR-12.core_idea: VWAP is the day's institutional cost basis; when price stretches multiple standard deviations away, mean-reversion traders fade back toward it, exploiting the same pull that execution algos exert. Implementations typically require the deviation to be volatility-normalized and avoid fading on breakout days (strong trend + news). The companion breakout use of VWAP belongs to VO-07/08.
MR-12.rules: Long when close < VWAP - 2 x rolling stdev of (close - VWAP) with no gap-news regime; exit at VWAP; short mirrored.
MR-12.key_parameters: Deviation window 20-50 bars; bands at 1-2 sigma; hard time-stop by session end.
MR-12.duplicates_eliminated: CN 分时VWAP回归; RU «откат к VWAP» скрипты; every VWAP-bands pack on TradingView.

MR-13.name: Z-Score Spread Reversion
MR-13.alt_names: Z分数价差回归 · Z-score возврат спреда
MR-13.origin: Academic stat-arb (Gatev et al. 1999; Avellaneda & Lee 2010) adapted to single-asset z-scores.
MR-13.core_idea: Standardize a price, spread, or indicator as a rolling z-score and trade crossings of +/-2 back toward zero, with sizing scaled by the z magnitude. On a pair spread it is pairs trading (ST-01); on a single asset's deviation from its own anchor (MA, VWAP, ratio to a lead) it is the general form of every band fade in this family. The z formulation is what makes threshold tuning transferable across assets.
MR-13.rules: Enter at z beyond +/-2 in the direction of reversion; exit at z = 0; hard stop at z = +/-3.5 (assumption break).
MR-13.key_parameters: Lookback 20-60 for the mean/sigma; half-life check via Ornstein-Uhlenbeck fit.
MR-13.duplicates_eliminated: RU «Z-score роботы»; CN 标准化偏离策略; Pairs-trading single-leg approximations.

MR-14.name: Williams %R Fade
MR-14.core_idea: A normalized stochastic that reads where close sits inside the recent high-low range; classic use fades readings beyond -80/-20 back toward the midrange. Williams himself is better known for volatility-breakout systems (C-Degree, OOPS), so the fade form is the community's usage rather than the author's own trading. It shares all the standard oscillator-fade caveats.
MR-14.rules: Long when %R crosses up through -80; exit at -50 or -20; short mirrored.
MR-14.duplicates_eliminated: RU %R-роботы; CN 威廉指标战法; bundled in every platform's default indicator set.

MR-15.name: Money-Flow Reversion (CMF/MFI)
MR-15.alt_names: 资金流回归 · Возврат по денежному потоку
MR-15.origin: Chaikin Money Flow / Accumulation-Distribution (Marc Chaikin, 1966-1980s); Money Flow Index (Quong & Soudack, 1989).
MR-15.core_idea: Volume-weighted oscillators score whether closing strength coincides with volume; readings at extremes with price not confirming signal absorption or climactic transfer. Mean-reversion implementations fade CMF/MFI extremes toward zero with a price-trend filter, treating the volume dimension as the edge over plain RSI fades.
MR-15.rules: Long when MFI(14) < 20 with price above its 200-MA; exit when MFI > 50; CMF variant uses +/-0.25 bands.
MR-15.duplicates_eliminated: CN 资金流指标策略; RU «денежный поток» индикаторные системы; OBV-family hybrids (cross VO-02).

BK-01.name: Opening Range Breakout (ORB)
BK-01.alt_names: 开盘区间突破 · Пробой диапазона открытия
BK-01.origin: Toby Crabel, Day Trading with Short Term Price Patterns and Opening Range Breakout (1990).
BK-01.core_idea: Define the high/low of the first 5-30 minutes and trade stops outside that range; the opening range encodes overnight information being repriced by the day's first liquidity wave. Crabel's statistical work on gap behavior underlies dozens of modern ORB variants, including the 2020s 'ORB-5' revival in US equities. Failure handling (re-entry, midpoint stops) matters more than the entry itself.
BK-01.rules: After the range closes, long on close above OR-high (stop on OR-low), short mirrored; flatten by session end.
BK-01.key_parameters: Range 5/15/30 minutes; stop at opposite edge or midpoint; skip inside days by volume filter.
BK-01.duplicates_eliminated: CN 开盘区间突破 (股票/股指); RU «Пробой открытия» intraday robots; ICT opening-range variants (cross PA-09).
BK-01.pine_code:
//@version=5
strategy("Opening Range Breakout (ORB)", overlay=true)
sess  = input.session("0930-0945", "Opening range session")
tz    = input.string("America/New_York", "Timezone")
inOR  = not na(time(timeframe.period, sess, tz))
var float orHi = na
var float orLo = na
newDay = ta.change(time("D")) != 0
if newDay
orHi := na
orLo := na
if inOR
orHi := na(orHi) ? high : math.max(orHi, high)
orLo := na(orLo) ? low  : math.min(orLo, low)
if not inOR and not na(orHi) and strategy.position_size == 0
if close > orHi
strategy.entry("L", strategy.long)
if close < orLo
strategy.entry("S", strategy.short)
if strategy.position_size > 0
strategy.exit("LX", from_entry="L", stop=orLo)
if strategy.position_size < 0
strategy.exit("SX", from_entry="S", stop=orHi)
if newDay
strategy.close_all(comment="Session reset")
plot(inOR ? orHi : na, "OR High", color=color.teal, style=plot.style_linebr)
plot(inOR ? orLo : na, "OR Low", color=color.red, style=plot.style_linebr)

BK-02.name: Narrow Range 7 / Inside Day Patterns
BK-02.alt_names: 窄幅整理形态 · Внутренний день / узкий диапазон
BK-02.origin: Toby Crabel (1990), building on 1970s floor-trader NR7 lore.
BK-02.core_idea: A day whose range is the narrowest of the last 7 (NR7), or an inside day fully engulfed by the prior bar, marks volatility contraction that statistically precedes expansion; trade the break of the contraction bar in either direction. Crabel's book remains the quantitative foundation of all 'compression day' trading. Modern VCP (BK-03) is the multi-stage generalization.
BK-02.rules: Next day, buy a stop above the NR7/inside-day high, sell a stop below its low; cancel the unfilled side after the first fill.
BK-02.key_parameters: NR7 (or NR4); ORB-style stops; ATR-scaled targets.
BK-02.duplicates_eliminated: CN 窄幅整理突破; RU 'узкий диапазон' scripts; ID/NR4 variants.

BK-03.name: Volatility Contraction Pattern (VCP)
BK-03.alt_names: 波动收缩形态 · Модель сжатия волатильности
BK-03.origin: Mark Minervini (2010s workshops/books); crowdsourced into Pine scanners.
BK-03.core_idea: Successive pullbacks within a base each get shallower (volume dries up in parallel) until a breakout with restored volume; the geometry is a volume-price handshake that supply is exhausted. The Pine form is a scan: decreasing range-depth stages plus a 10/50-bar volume dry-up, then a breakout trigger. It is the swing-trading descendant of Crabel's NR logic and O'Neil's base counts.
BK-03.rules: Detect 2-4 stages of contraction (depth_n < depth_n-1); arm on volume dry-up; enter on close above contraction high with volume > 1.5x 50-bar average.
BK-03.key_parameters: Base 50-65 bars; 3 stages typical; volume surge 1.5-2x.
BK-03.duplicates_eliminated: Minervini scan packs; Qullamägi EP/gap momentum (cousin); CN 强势股缩量整理突破.
BK-03.pine_code:
//@version=5
indicator("VCP Contraction Scan", overlay=true)
lookback = input.int(60, "Base lookback")
stages   = input.int(3, "Contraction stages")
seg = int(lookback / stages)
depth(k) => (ta.highest(high, k) - ta.lowest(low, k)) / ta.lowest(low, k) * 100
d1 = depth(seg)
d2 = depth(seg * 2)
d3 = depth(seg * 3)
contracting = d1 < d2 and d2 < d3
dryUp = ta.sma(volume, 10) < 0.6 * ta.sma(volume, 50)
breakout = close > ta.highest(high, seg)[1] and volume > 1.5 * ta.sma(volume, 50)
plotshape(contracting and dryUp, "Contraction + dry-up", shape.circle,
location.belowbar, color=color.orange, size=size.tiny)
plotshape(breakout and contracting[1], "Breakout", shape.triangleup,
location.belowbar, color=color.teal, size=size.small)

BK-04.name: Darvas Box
BK-04.origin: Nicolas Darvas, 1959 Barron's articles; How I Made $2,000,000 in the Stock Market (1960).
BK-04.core_idea: After three consecutive higher highs form a 'box top' and a failing pullback forms the box bottom, buy the breakout of the top and trail the stop under the most recent box bottom; each new consolidation draws a new box. It is trend following on a dancer's travel schedule — Darvas famously ran it by telegram from nightclubs. Mechanically it is a swing-anchored Donchian with human box-drawing rules.
BK-04.rules: Box from 3-day top / bottom definition; enter on close above box top; stop under box bottom; pyramid into new boxes.
BK-04.key_parameters: 3-day box (classic); volume confirmation optional; stop = last box bottom.
BK-04.duplicates_eliminated: CN 箱体突破; RU «Метод Дарваса»; box-drawing scripts across all platforms.

BK-05.name: Bill Williams Alligator + Fractals
BK-05.alt_names: 比尔·威廉姆斯鳄鱼线+分形 · Аллигатор и фракталы Вильямса
BK-05.origin: Bill Williams, Trading Chaos (1995) and New Trading Dimensions (1998).
BK-05.core_idea: Three smoothed MAs (13/8/5 of the median price, displaced forward) form the Alligator: when the lines fan out in order the 'alligator is eating' and fractal breakouts may be traded in that direction; when they interweave, sleep and stand aside. Up/down fractals (5-bar extremes) supply entry triggers. No system better symbolizes the 1990s-2000s retail era — and none has a larger Russian following.
BK-05.rules: Long when the Alligator is aligned up and close breaks the most recent up-fractal; short mirrored; exit on Alligator interweave or opposite fractal.
BK-05.key_parameters: SMMA 13/8/5 with 8/5/3 forward displacement; fractal 5-bar pivots.
BK-05.duplicates_eliminated: RU «Аллигатор Вильямса» robots (enormous MQL4/5 corpus); CN 鳄鱼线战法; Awesome/AC oscillator combos (BK-06).
BK-05.pine_code:
//@version=5
strategy("Alligator + Fractal Breakout", overlay=true)
jaw   = ta.rma(hl2, 13)
teeth = ta.rma(hl2, 8)
lip   = ta.rma(hl2, 5)
alignedUp = lip > teeth and teeth > jaw
alignedDn = lip < teeth and teeth < jaw
upFr = ta.pivothigh(high, 2, 2)
dnFr = ta.pivotlow(low, 2, 2)
var float lastUpFr = na
var float lastDnFr = na
if not na(upFr)
lastUpFr := upFr
if not na(dnFr)
lastDnFr := dnFr
if alignedUp and not na(lastUpFr) and close > lastUpFr and strategy.position_size <= 0
strategy.entry("L", strategy.long)
if alignedDn and not na(lastDnFr) and close < lastDnFr and strategy.position_size >= 0
strategy.entry("S", strategy.short)
plot(jaw, "Jaw", color=color.blue, offset=8)
plot(teeth, "Teeth", color=color.red, offset=5)
plot(lip, "Lip", color=color.green, offset=3)

BK-06.name: Awesome Oscillator / Accelerator System
BK-06.alt_names: 神奇震荡指标系统 · Система по AO/AC
BK-06.core_idea: The Awesome Oscillator (SMA(34) - SMA(5) of median price) signals via 'saucer' patterns, twin peaks, and zero-line crosses; the Accelerator adds momentum-of-momentum. Used with the Alligator it filters entries to trend direction. Mechanically it is a slow-fast MA spread oscillator — a MACD cousin — which is why standalone AO systems mostly duplicate MACD logic under new vocabulary.
BK-06.rules: Long on AO saucer-above-zero or zero-line cross up, in Alligator-up regime; short mirrored.
BK-06.duplicates_eliminated: RU «Система Билла Вильямса» full-suite robots; CN AO/AC战法; MACD-equivalent logic (cross TR-05).

BK-07.name: Aroon Breakout
BK-07.alt_names: 阿隆指标突破 · Система по Aroon
BK-07.core_idea: Aroon Up/Down measure bars since the recent 25-bar high/low; crossovers near the top of their range flag fresh trend leadership. As a breakout proxy it is slower than Donchian but immune to close-versus-intrabar ambiguity. It sees periodic revivals in scan-oriented communities but rarely stands alone in production.
BK-07.rules: Long when Aroon-Up crosses above Aroon-Down above 70; exit on reverse cross or drop below 50.
BK-07.duplicates_eliminated: Aroon cross robots on MQL5; CN 阿隆指标 templates.

BK-08.name: Range Breakout with Volume Surge (放量突破)
BK-08.alt_names: 放量突破平台 · Пробой флэта с объёмом
BK-08.origin: Universal TA; formalized in CN platform templates (通达信/同花顺 放量突破 formulas) and JoinQuant volume-confirm strategies.
BK-08.core_idea: Breakouts validated by abnormal volume fail less: the entry demands both a new N-bar high and volume above k times its moving average, tying the break to real participation. Chinese retail materials treat this as the canonical platform-breakout (平台突破) filter, and it is the volume layer that most western breakout systems add informally.
BK-08.rules: Long on close above N-bar high with volume > k x SMA(volume,20); stop under the range low; trail after 1R.
BK-08.key_parameters: N 20-60; k 1.5-2.5; range depth filter optional.
BK-08.duplicates_eliminated: BK-09 consolidation breakout; RU «пробой с объёмом»; OBV/CMF breakout hybrids.

BK-09.name: Consolidation Box Breakout
BK-09.alt_names: 平台整理突破 · Пробой боковика
BK-09.origin: Classic swing methodology; CN platform-era formalization (平台突破战法).
BK-09.core_idea: Identify a sideways box of at least N bars with contracting range, then trade the close outside the box with volume confirmation. Unlike Darvas (BK-04) it does not require the prior uptrend geometry, so it is the generic form used on any instrument. The statistical justification is identical to NR7: compression precedes expansion.
BK-09.rules: Box = highest/lowest over N bars with range < x% of price; long on close above box high + volume filter; stop at box midpoint.
BK-09.duplicates_eliminated: CN 平台突破/整理突破; RU «пробой консолидации»; Darvas and NR7 (same mechanism).

BK-10.name: Gap Playbook (Fade / Continue)
BK-10.alt_names: 跳空缺口策略 · Стратегии гэпов
BK-10.origin: Crabel's gap statistics (1990); institutionalized in US equities; MOEX dividend-gap practice (RU-07) is a special case.
BK-10.core_idea: Classify opening gaps by size against ATR and by cause: small technical gaps in trend direction tend to continue, while large exhaustion gaps into resistance tend to fill. The systematic form trades the first 15-30 minutes' failure or confirmation of the gap. Full-measure and runaway gaps are excluded from fading.
BK-10.rules: Fade: short gap-ups > 0.5 ATR into resistance after a weak first hour; continue: enter with the gap when the open drives further within 15 minutes.
BK-10.key_parameters: Gap size 0.25-1.0 ATR buckets; confirmation window 15-30 min; stop beyond gap extreme.
BK-10.duplicates_eliminated: CN 缺口回补策略; RU гэп-роботы; ORB gap variants (cross BK-01).

BK-11.name: Squeeze Pro / Multi-Threshold Squeeze
BK-11.alt_names: 多档挤压指标 · Squeeze Pro
BK-11.origin: LuxAlgo (2020-2023 open library), extending TTM Squeeze (MR-05).
BK-11.core_idea: Grades compression into low/mid/high squeeze levels by comparing Bollinger-to-Keltner distance against historical thresholds, giving a severity ladder rather than a binary flag. Traders arm alerts at high squeeze and trade the release. Functionally it is TTM Squeeze with a calibrated intensity scale — kept as a distinct entry because its release logic differs.
BK-11.rules: Alert on high-squeeze; enter on squeeze release in the direction of the momentum histogram; scale position by squeeze grade.
BK-11.key_parameters: BB/KC as TTM; percentile thresholds 0.5/1.0/1.5 sigma of band separation.
BK-11.duplicates_eliminated: TTM Squeeze (MR-05) as the parent; LazyBear Hi-Lo squeezes; CN 多档收口实验性 scripts.

BK-12.name: High-of-Day Break & Retest
BK-12.alt_names: 日内新高突破回踩 · Пробой максимума дня с ретестом
BK-12.origin: Intraday momentum practice (2000s prop desks); formalized in community scripts.
BK-12.core_idea: When price takes out the morning's high after consolidation, enter on the retest of that broken level rather than the break itself, cutting the false-break rate at the cost of missing runners. The retest requirement is the key differentiator from raw ORB-style momentum. Often combined with VWAP-relative position filters.
BK-12.rules: Long on pullback touching the broken HOD with a bullish reversal bar; stop under retest low; target 1.5-2R or EOD.
BK-12.key_parameters: HOD window from open; retest tolerance 0.1-0.2 ATR; VWAP filter.
BK-12.duplicates_eliminated: CN 日内新高策略; RU intraday HOD scripts; IB opening-drive variants.

BK-13.name: Volatility Expansion Breakout (Keltner/ATR form)
BK-13.alt_names: 波动扩张突破 · Пробой расширения волатильности
BK-13.origin: Chester Keltner's envelope re-cast as a breakout by Linda Raschke and vn.py's KingKeltner template.
BK-13.core_idea: Instead of fading the Keltner envelope (MR-04), trade stops outside it: close beyond EMA(20) + 2 x ATR(10) signals expansion worth following. This is the CTA workhorse form — the vn.py KingKeltnerStrategy is exactly this on Chinese futures. It pairs naturally with ADX gates to avoid trendless expansion noise.
BK-13.rules: Long on close above upper band; exit on close back inside the channel or a trailing 3 x ATR stop; short mirrored.
BK-13.key_parameters: EMA 20, ATR 10, multiple 2-2.5; optional ADX > 20 gate.
BK-13.duplicates_eliminated: vn.py KingKeltnerStrategy; CN 肯特纳突破 CTA templates; RU канальные пробойные роботы.

PA-01.name: Wyckoff Accumulation/Distribution & Spring (V-Hook)
PA-01.alt_names: 威科夫吸筹与弹簧效应 · Метод Вайкоффа
PA-01.origin: Richard D. Wyckoff, Stock Market Institute course materials (1931-1934); schematics formalized later by Bob Evans.
PA-01.core_idea: Markets accumulate in ranges where the composite operator absorbs supply; the spring is the deliberate shakeout below the range that sweeps resting stops before markup — the upthrust mirrors it in distribution. The mechanical form trades a defined range: sweep beyond the low by up to ~1 ATR on a volume spike, then reclaim of the range low, with stops outside the sweep. Every liquidity-sweep method in this glossary is downstream of this idea.
PA-01.rules: Define a 20-40 bar range; long on a low piercing range-low by <= 1 ATR that closes back inside with volume > 1.5x average; stop below sweep low; targets at range high then measured move.
PA-01.key_parameters: Range lookback 20-40; depth cap 1.0-1.2 ATR; volume multiple 1.5-2.5; phase filters optional.
PA-01.duplicates_eliminated: Wyckoff [theUltimator5] schematic indicator; CN 威科夫吸筹 materials; RU Вайкофф course translations; Linda Raschke's Turtle Soup (PA-10) is the fade-cousin; this workspace's V-Hook agent is a direct implementation.
PA-01.pine_code:
//@version=5
strategy("Wyckoff Spring / Upthrust (V-Hook)", overlay=true)
rangeLen = input.int(30, "Range lookback")
depthMax = input.float(1.0, "Max sweep depth (ATR)")
volMult  = input.float(1.5, "Volume multiple")
rngHi = ta.highest(high, rangeLen)[1]
rngLo = ta.lowest(low, rangeLen)[1]
atr   = ta.atr(14)
flat    = (rngHi - rngLo) / rngLo < 0.15
swept   = low < rngLo and rngLo - low <= depthMax * atr and close > rngLo
upthrust = flat and high > rngHi and high - rngHi <= depthMax * atr and close < rngHi
volSpike = volume > volMult * ta.sma(volume, 20)
spring = flat and swept and volSpike
if spring
strategy.entry("L", strategy.long)
if upthrust and volSpike
strategy.entry("S", strategy.short)
if strategy.position_size > 0 and close < rngLo - 2 * atr
strategy.close("L", comment="Failed spring")
if strategy.position_size < 0 and close > rngHi + 2 * atr
strategy.close("S", comment="Failed upthrust")
plot(rngHi, "Range high", color=color.new(color.teal, 40))
plot(rngLo, "Range low", color=color.new(color.red, 40))

PA-02.name: Effort vs Result / Composite Operator Reading
PA-02.alt_names: 量价背离的威科夫读法 · Соотнесение усилия и результата
PA-02.origin: Wyckoff course lineage; teaching tradition via Bob Evans' 'effort vs result' papers.
PA-02.core_idea: Compare the effort (spread and volume of a bar or swing) with the result (price progress): big effort with no progress signals absorption by the other side, small effort with large progress signals a vacuum of opposing orders. These are the diagnostic sentences of Wyckoff analysis; mechanically they appear as volume-spread anomalies that gate other entries rather than standalone signals.
PA-02.rules: Flag bars in the top decile of volume with bottom-quartile progress; use as entry/exit confluence for PA-01 or VO-01 systems.
PA-02.key_parameters: Volume percentile 90; progress normalized by ATR.
PA-02.duplicates_eliminated: VSA (VO-01) is the formalized descendant; CN 量价背离 reading; RU «усилие-результат» school.

PA-03.name: Pin Bar / Hammer Rejection
PA-03.origin: Candlestick lineage (Homma, 18th c.; Nison's 1991 westernization); 'pin bar' term popularized by Martin Cole and Nial Fuller (2000s).
PA-03.core_idea: A long-tailed bar whose close sits near the opposite extreme shows a one-sided auction that was rejected; trading the close beyond the bar's nose in the rejection direction captures the failure of the sweep. The pattern is a single-bar Wyckoff spring and is the most-taught retail setup in Russian and English-language price-action schools alike.
PA-03.rules: Long when a lower-wick >= 2x body bar closes in the upper third after a downswing; enter above its high; stop below the wick.
PA-03.key_parameters: Tail/body ratio 2:1; trend context filter (EMA 50/200); 1-2R targets.
PA-03.duplicates_eliminated: RU «пинбар» schools (every RU PA course); CN 长下影/锤子线战法; hammer/shooting-star mechanical scripts.

PA-04.name: Engulfing & Inside-Bar Momentum Patterns
PA-04.alt_names: 吞没与内包形态 · Паттерны поглощения и внутреннего бара
PA-04.origin: Japanese candlestick canon; Steve Nison, Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques (1991).
PA-04.core_idea: An engulfing bar completesly absorbs the prior bar's body, marking a decisive swing of control; the inside bar marks compression that resolves in the direction of the break. Both are the atomic units from which larger setups (fakey, ORB, Wyckoff) are assembled, and they backtest best with a trend filter and volume confirmation rather than standalone.
PA-04.rules: Long on bullish engulfing above EMA(50); stop 1.5 ATR; optional inside-bar break continuation entry.
PA-04.key_parameters: Body-based definition (wicks excluded); trend filter EMA 50/200.
PA-04.duplicates_eliminated: MT4 engulfing EAs; CN 阳包阴战法; RU «поглощение» robots.
PA-04.pine_code:
//@version=5
strategy("Engulfing with Trend Filter", overlay=true)
bodyUp = close > open and close[1] < open[1] and close >= open[1] and open <= close[1]
bodyDn = close < open and close[1] > open[1] and close <= open[1] and open >= close[1]
upTrend = close > ta.ema(close, 50)
dnTrend = close < ta.ema(close, 50)
atr = ta.atr(14)
if bodyUp and upTrend
strategy.entry("L", strategy.long)
if bodyDn and dnTrend
strategy.entry("S", strategy.short)
if strategy.position_size > 0 and close < strategy.position_avg_price - 1.5 * atr
strategy.close("L", comment="Stop")
if strategy.position_size < 0 and close > strategy.position_avg_price + 1.5 * atr
strategy.close("S", comment="Stop")

PA-05.name: Al Brooks Bar-by-Bar Price Action
PA-05.alt_names: 布鲁克斯逐K线价格行为 · Прайс-экшн по Бруксу
PA-05.origin: Al Brooks, Reading Price Charts Bar by Bar (2009) and the Brooks Trading Course (2011+).
PA-05.core_idea: A complete grammar of 5-minute charts: every bar is a setup candidate, with high-1/low-1 to high-4/low-4 counted entries in pullbacks, second-entry doctrine, measured-move targets, and always-in direction. It is the most internally consistent retail price-action system ever published, though its full context-dependence resists complete mechanization; partial Pine ports implement the counted entries and always-in flip.
PA-05.rules: In a bull trend, buy the first pullback to the EMA-20 that forms a bull bar (H1); re-enter on H2/H3 after failed attempts; always-in flips on strong reversal bars.
PA-05.key_parameters: EMA 20 anchor; 5-minute or daily charts; scalper's entry/exit or swing variant.
PA-05.duplicates_eliminated: Brooks-method scan scripts; RU «бар-за баром» translations; second-entry fan implementations.

PA-06.name: Fakey / False-Breakout Inside-Bar
PA-06.alt_names: 假突破内包形态 · Фейки (ложный пробой)
PA-06.origin: Popularized by Nial Fuller's price-action courses (2000s); mechanism identical to Wyckoff's upthrust-after-pullback.
PA-06.core_idea: An inside bar followed by a false break of the mother bar that closes back inside creates a two-sided liquidity trap: breakout traders are trapped and their stops fuel the reversal. Trading the close back through the mother-bar edge turns the trap into an entry with a naturally tight stop behind the false extreme.
PA-06.rules: Detect inside bar; on a false break beyond the mother bar that closes back inside, enter the reversal; stop beyond the false extreme.
PA-06.key_parameters: Mother bar 1-3 bars; breakout tolerance 1-2 ticks; trend filter recommended.
PA-06.duplicates_eliminated: Turtle Soup (PA-10); stop-run/'spoofy' scripts; RU «ложный пробой» scripts.

PA-07.name: Supply & Demand Zones (Set-and-Forget)
PA-07.alt_names: 供需区域策略 · Зоны спроса и предложения
PA-07.origin: Sam Seiden (2000s webinars, 'supply and demand' rebranding of S/R); hundreds of open Pine implementations.
PA-07.core_idea: A strong one-way move leaving a small consolidation ('base') defines a zone where institutional orders rested; price's first return to the zone is traded for a continuation, on the theory that unfilled institutional interest remains. The mechanical core is a rally-base-rally or drop-base-drop detector plus a retest trigger. It is the retail-popular cousin of order-block logic (PA-08).
PA-07.rules: Detect base (low-range bars) followed by impulse > 1.5 ATR; mark zone as base high/low; enter on first retest; stop beyond zone.
PA-07.key_parameters: Base 1-5 bars; impulse 1.5-2 ATR; zone validity 1-3 touches.
PA-07.duplicates_eliminated: Order block overlaps (PA-08); CN 供需区域 scripts; RU «зоны спроса/предложения» packs.
PA-07.pine_code:
//@version=5
strategy("Supply-Demand Zone Retest", overlay=true)
impulse  = input.float(1.5, "Impulse ATR multiple")
baseBars = input.int(3, "Base bars")
atr = ta.atr(14)
baseFlat = math.abs(ta.highest(high, baseBars) - ta.lowest(low, baseBars)) < atr
bullBase = baseFlat[1] and close - close[baseBars] > impulse * atr
bearBase = baseFlat[1] and close[baseBars] - close > impulse * atr
var float dzTop = na
var float dzBot = na
var float szTop = na
var float szBot = na
if bullBase
dzTop := ta.highest(high, baseBars)[1]
dzBot := ta.lowest(low, baseBars)[1]
if bearBase
szTop := ta.highest(high, baseBars)[1]
szBot := ta.lowest(low, baseBars)[1]
demandRetest = not na(dzBot) and low <= dzTop and close > dzBot and strategy.position_size <= 0
supplyRetest = not na(szTop) and high >= szBot and close < szTop and strategy.position_size >= 0
if demandRetest
strategy.entry("L", strategy.long)
if supplyRetest
strategy.entry("S", strategy.short)
plot(dzTop, "Demand top", color=color.teal, style=plot.style_linebr)
plot(dzBot, "Demand bottom", color=color.teal, style=plot.style_linebr)
plot(szTop, "Supply top", color=color.red, style=plot.style_linebr)
plot(szBot, "Supply bottom", color=color.red, style=plot.style_linebr)

PA-08.name: Smart Money Concepts (BOS / CHoCH / Order Blocks / FVG)
PA-08.alt_names: 聪明钱结构交易 · Умные деньги (SMC)
PA-08.origin: LuxAlgo 'Smart Money Concepts' open script (2021+, most-starred of its genre), systematizing ICT vocabulary (see PA-09).
PA-08.core_idea: SMC formalizes structure trading: a Break of Structure confirms trend continuation, a Change of Character flags reversal, order blocks mark the last opposing candle before an impulsive displacement (institutional footprint), and Fair Value Gaps are 3-bar imbalances expected to refill. The mechanical trade is: structure break defines bias, then a retrace into the order block or FVG is the entry. Its popularity makes it the defining retail framework of the 2020s.
PA-08.rules: Swing pivots define structure; on a bullish BOS mark the last bearish candle before displacement as the OB; long on first retrace into the OB while bias holds; CHoCH invalidates.
PA-08.key_parameters: Swing length 5-15; displacement filter 1-1.5 ATR; OB expiry on full mitigation.
PA-08.duplicates_eliminated: LuxAlgo SMC [ML] and dozens of forks; ICT order-block scripts; CN 主力结构 (SMART概念) scripts; RU SMC переводы — the framework is one concept despite hundreds of branded scripts.
PA-08.pine_code:
//@version=5
strategy("SMC: BOS + Order Block Retrace", overlay=true)
swingLen = input.int(10, "Swing length")
ph = ta.pivothigh(high, swingLen, swingLen)
pl = ta.pivotlow(low, swingLen, swingLen)
var float lastHigh = na
var float lastLow = na
var int bias = 0
var float obTop = na
var float obBot = na
if not na(ph)
lastHigh := ph
if not na(pl)
lastLow := pl
if not na(lastHigh) and close > lastHigh and nz(bias[1]) <= 0
bias := 1
obTop := lastHigh
obBot := ta.lowest(low, swingLen)
if not na(lastLow) and close < lastLow and nz(bias[1]) >= 0
bias := -1
obTop := ta.highest(high, swingLen)
obBot := lastLow
retraceLong  = bias == 1 and not na(obBot) and low <= obTop and close > obBot
retraceShort = bias == -1 and not na(obTop) and high >= obBot and close < obTop
if retraceLong
strategy.entry("L", strategy.long)
if retraceShort
strategy.entry("S", strategy.short)
plot(bias == 1 ? obTop : na, "Bull OB top", color=color.teal, style=plot.style_linebr)
plot(bias == 1 ? obBot : na, "Bull OB bottom", color=color.teal, style=plot.style_linebr)
plot(bias == -1 ? obTop : na, "Bear OB top", color=color.red, style=plot.style_linebr)
plot(bias == -1 ? obBot : na, "Bear OB bottom", color=color.red, style=plot.style_linebr)

PA-09.name: ICT Kill Zones, Silver Bullet & Time-Based Liquidity
PA-09.alt_names: ICT时区流动性策略 · ICT Килл-зоны
PA-09.origin: Michael J. Huddleston, 'The Inner Circle Trader' (2010s free/core courses; massive 2020s revival).
PA-09.core_idea: ICT maps institutional session rhythms: London and New York 'kill zones' carry the day's real liquidity events; the Silver Bullet is a 10:00-11:00 ET window where a specific FVG continuation setup repeats; Judas swings are early session fake moves that set up the true move. The edge claimed is time-conditional liquidity, making it a session family (SE) wearing price-action clothes.
PA-09.rules: During the defined window, enter on FVG/OB retrace in the direction of the session's initial sweep reversal; fixed R targets.
PA-09.key_parameters: Kill zones 02:00-05:00 and 08:30-11:00 ET; Silver Bullet 10:00-11:00 ET; 2-6R targets.
PA-09.duplicates_eliminated: ICT concepts scripts (dozens); PA-08 SMC (shared vocabulary); SE-01 Asia-range sweep (shared mechanism).

PA-10.name: Turtle Soup / Fake Breakout Fade
PA-10.alt_names: 海龟汤反向策略 · Контрпробой 'Turtle Soup'
PA-10.origin: Linda Bradford Raschke & Larry Connors, Street Smarts (1995).
PA-10.core_idea: A deliberate anti-Donchian: when price breaks a 20-day high/low but fails to hold for one bar, fade the failure back into the range. Raschke's joke was that buying Donchian breakouts had become so popular that fading them fed on the crowd. It works best when the failure bar also sweeps an obvious stop cluster — the same auction logic as the Wyckoff spring in reverse time order.
PA-10.rules: Short when price takes out the 20-day high intraday but closes back below it; enter on the next bar, stop above the failure extreme, target the range mid.
PA-10.key_parameters: 20-day extremes (or 55); one-bar failure rule; 50% range target.
PA-10.duplicates_eliminated: Fakey (PA-06); 'stop hunt fade' scripts; CN 假突破反打.

PA-11.name: Harmonic Patterns (Gartley / Bat / Butterfly / AB=CD)
PA-11.origin: H.M. Gartley, Profits in the Stock Market (1935); Fibonacci ratios and XABCD formalization by Larry Pesavento (1990s) and Scott Carney, The Harmonic Trader (1998).
PA-11.core_idea: Specific Fibonacci retracement/extension relationships between five swing points (X-A-B-C-D) define reversal geometries: the Gartley's B-point at 0.618 XA with D at 0.786, the Bat, the Butterfly's 1.27 XA extension, and the simpler AB=CD. Trades enter at the D completion with stops beyond the pattern's invalidation ratio. Mechanization requires robust pivot detection and ratio tolerance, which is why most implementations are indicators, not strategies.
PA-11.rules: Detect XABCD pivots; verify ratio windows (e.g., Gartley: B 0.618 +/- 0.05 XA, D 0.786 XA); enter at D, stop beyond X.
PA-11.duplicates_eliminated: Pesavento vs Carney naming disputes (same patterns); RU «Гартли/летучая мышь» packs; CN 谐波形态 scripts.

PA-12.name: Elliott Wave (Mechanized Approaches)
PA-12.alt_names: 艾略特波浪（机械化） · Волны Эллиотта
PA-12.origin: Ralph Nelson Elliott, The Wave Principle (1938); mechanization attempts since the 1980s software era.
PA-12.core_idea: Five-wave impulse and three-wave correction fractals, with wave 3 never the shortest and wave 4 not overlapping wave 1's territory. Fully automatic wave counting is famously ambiguous, so practical implementations use zigzag pivots with degree nesting to propose counts and trade the wave-4-to-5 continuation or the C-wave terminal. It endures as an analytical overlay more than a standalone strategy.
PA-12.rules: Zigzag pivots propose counts; long the pivot after a qualifying wave-4 low targeting wave-5 projection; invalidation on overlap.
PA-12.key_parameters: Zigzag deviation 3-10%; Fibonacci projections 0.618/1.0/1.618 of wave 1.
PA-12.duplicates_eliminated: RU Эллиотт-школы (large following); CN 波浪理论 automated drafts; every 'EW auto-count' indicator.

PA-13.name: Wolfe Waves
PA-13.origin: Brian and Bill Wolfe, early 1990s (published as a paid course; later widely redistributed).
PA-13.core_idea: A 5-point pattern where waves 1-4 bound an equilibrating channel and wave 5 overshoots a projected 'line' extension, targeting a natural-path reversal toward point 1-4 convergence. It is essentially a corrective wedge with a projected termination line, traded at the wave-5 extreme with a tight stop. Popularity concentrated in forex forums and RU/EN script libraries.
PA-13.rules: Detect 5 alternating pivots with 1-4 channel geometry; enter at wave-5 line touch; target the 1-4 ray.
PA-13.key_parameters: Pivot detection zigzag 3-8%; target = 1-4 line projection.
PA-13.duplicates_eliminated: Wolfe Wave scripts on MQL5/TradingView; RU «волны Вольфа» robots.

PA-14.name: Classical Reversal Patterns Automated (Double Top, H&S)
PA-14.alt_names: 经典反转形态自动化 · Автоматизация классических паттернов
PA-14.origin: Schabacker (1932), Edwards & Magee (1948) — the archive canon; automation via pivot libraries.
PA-14.core_idea: Double tops/bottoms and head-and-shoulders are detected from swing pivots: two comparable extremes separated by a trough, or three extremes with a middle head, completed on a neckline break. Automated detection mainly serves as a scanner for discretionary traders; as mechanical entries they suffer from pattern-boundary ambiguity, so implementations tune pivot sensitivity heavily.
PA-14.rules: Detect pivots; H&S short on neckline break with stop above right shoulder; target = pattern height projected from the break.
PA-14.key_parameters: Pivot strength 5-10; peak similarity tolerance 2-5%; neckline slope filter.
PA-14.duplicates_eliminated: CN 双头双底/头肩顶 scripts; RU «голова-плечи» роботы; every platform's built-in pattern detection.

PA-15.name: Trendline & Channel Break Automation
PA-15.alt_names: 趋势线突破自动化 · Автопробой трендовых линий
PA-15.origin: Manual TA since Dow; automated by linreg channels (Ehlers-era) and pivot-line fitting scripts.
PA-15.core_idea: Fit a line through at least two (ideally three) pivot highs/lows and trade closes beyond it, or trade the linear-regression channel's outer bands as dynamic trendlines. Automation exposes the subjectivity problem: touch tolerance and fit window dominate results. The linreg-channel form is the most reproducible and pairs with R-squared as a fit-quality gate.
PA-15.rules: Long on close above a downsloping line drawn through 2+ pivot lows, with rising R-squared; stop beyond the last pivot.
PA-15.key_parameters: Fit window 50-150 bars; touch tolerance 0.2 ATR; R-squared > 0.6 gate.
PA-15.duplicates_eliminated: RU «пробой трендовой» роботы; CN 趋势线突破 scripts; linreg channel packs.

PA-16.name: Round Numbers / Psychological Levels
PA-16.origin: Institutional limit-order clustering observations (1990s microstructure research); retail codification in forex communities.
PA-16.core_idea: Prices ending in zeros (and in CN/JPY contexts, fives) attract limit orders and stops, producing magnet-then-reject behavior; systematic approaches fade first touches of fresh round levels in ranges or use them as profit targets for momentum trades. Microstructure studies confirm clustering in FX and equities, making this one of the few patterns with clean academic support at the order-book level.
PA-16.rules: Define level = round(close, step); fade first touch when range regime; or place targets at the next level in trend regime.
PA-16.key_parameters: Step = 1/2/10/100 by asset; first-touch-only rule; ATR distance filter.
PA-16.duplicates_eliminated: CN 整数关口战法; RU «круглые цифры» robots; FX 'big figure' trading.

IH-01.name: MESA Adaptive MA (MAMA / FAMA)
IH-01.origin: John Ehlers, Rocket Science for Traders (2001); MESA trademark line.
IH-01.core_idea: A Hilbert-transform cycle measurement continuously retunes an EMA: when cycles are strong the MAMA tracks price closely, and the FAMA (MAMA of MAMA) trails as the signal line. Crosses of MAMA and FAMA generate signals that self-adjust to the dominant cycle length. It is the flagship of Ehlers' adaptive-filter program, though the full implementation is intricate enough that many ports approximate the phase calculation.
IH-01.rules: Long on MAMA crossing above FAMA; short mirrored; cycle period gate optional.
IH-01.duplicates_eliminated: MAMA/FAMA ports (TradeStation->MT4->Pine); CN 自适应均线 experiments.

IH-02.name: Instantaneous Trendline & Sine Wave
IH-02.alt_names: 瞬时趋势线与正弦波 · Мгновенная линия тренда
IH-02.origin: John Ehlers, Rocket Science for Traders (2001).
IH-02.core_idea: The Hilbert transform's dominant-cycle phase drives a sine wave that leads price into turns; when the phase line is clean, sine-vs-leadline crosses time reversals, and when the market is trending the tool itself says 'do not use me'. That self-aware regime flag is the sophisticated part: Ehlers explicitly gates the oscillator by trend detection. The instantaneous trendline (a phaser-corrected smoothing) is the companion trend measure.
IH-02.rules: Trade sine/leadline crosses only when the trend-mode flag is off; stand aside otherwise.
IH-02.key_parameters: Standard Hilbert constants; smoothing length ~7 for the trendline.
IH-02.duplicates_eliminated: Ehlers book-code ports; MT4/MT5 Hilbert suites.

IH-03.name: Cyber Cycle
IH-03.origin: John Ehlers, Cybernetic Analysis for Stocks and Futures (2004).
IH-03.core_idea: A two-pole high-pass filter that isolates the cycle component of price with minimal lag, then smooths it; crossovers with a trigger mark cycle turns. Ehlers positioned it as the clean cycle-extraction baseline against which more complex MESA work is judged. Its simplicity makes it one of the most-ported Ehlers tools.
IH-03.rules: Long on cycle crossing above trigger from a trough; short mirrored; skip signals when the trend component dominates.
IH-03.duplicates_eliminated: Ports in the Ehlers TASC archive; CN 循环指标 experiments.

IH-04.name: Ehlers SuperSmoother / Roofing Filter
IH-04.origin: John Ehlers, 'Predictive and Dedicated Indicators' (TASC 2013); roofing filter introduced with it.
IH-04.core_idea: The SuperSmoother is a two-pole Butterworth-style filter that removes aliasing noise far better than an EMA of equal length — Ehlers recommends it as the default replacement for every EMA in older systems. The roofing filter cascades a high-pass and SuperSmoother to feed clean data into cycle indicators. As a system it is a component, but its adoption fixed a generation of indicator quality.
IH-04.rules: Substitute SuperSmoother for EMA/SMA in any trend system; use roofing-filter output for cycle indicators.
IH-04.duplicates_eliminated: SuperSmoother ports everywhere; CN 超平滑滤波 scripts.
IH-04.pine_code:
//@version=5
indicator("Ehlers SuperSmoother", overlay=true)
len = input.int(10, "Length")
price = hl2
a1 = math.exp(-1.414 * 3.14159 / len)
b1 = 2.0 * a1 * math.cos(1.414 * 3.14159 / len)
c2 = b1
c3 = -a1 * a1
c1 = 1.0 - c2 - c3
var float ss = na
ss := c1 * (price + nz(price[1])) / 2.0 + c2 * nz(ss[1]) + c3 * nz(ss[2])
plot(ss, "SuperSmoother", color=color.teal)

IH-05.name: Vortex Indicator
IH-05.origin: Etienne Botes & Douglas Siepman, TASC January 2010, inspired by Hans Hannula's vortex concept and water vortex dynamics.
IH-05.core_idea: VI+ sums upward true-motion (high to prior low) and VI- the downward mirror, each normalized by true range; VI+ crossing above VI- marks trend initiation, sustained separation marks trend health. It was explicitly designed to catch the start of trends faster than DMI while sharing its normalization philosophy. A compact, well-specified system that ports perfectly.
IH-05.rules: Long on VI+ crossing above VI-; exit on reverse cross or VI+ falling below 1.0 from a high.
