ST-03.core_idea: Instead of a static OLS hedge ratio, a Kalman filter treats the ratio as a hidden state evolving with noise, adapting intra-sample as the relationship drifts — materially reducing spread blowups from ratio drift. The filter's innovation variance doubles as a regime alarm. It is the standard upgrade path for ST-01 implementations.
ST-03.rules: State = [alpha, beta] evolving as random walk; observation = pair prices; enter on standardized innovation bands; exit at mean.
ST-03.key_parameters: Process noise 1e-5..1e-3; observation noise from residuals; band 2 sigma of innovation.

ST-04.name: Cross-Sectional Momentum (Jegadeesh-Titman)
ST-04.alt_names: 横截面动量因子 · Кросс-секционный моментум
ST-04.origin: Narasimhan Jegadeesh & Sheridan Titman, Journal of Finance 1993.
ST-04.core_idea: Rank stocks by trailing 3-12 month returns, long the top decile short the bottom, skip the most recent month; winners outperform for 3-12 months. The most replicated anomaly in finance, present in nearly every market studied (with the notable CN exception where reversal historically dominated). It powers CN-12 sector rotation and TR-17's time-series cousin.
ST-04.rules: Rank by 12-1 month return; long top decile (or quintile), monthly rebalance; optional industry/size neutralization.
ST-04.key_parameters: Lookback 3-12 months; skip 1 month; decile portfolios.
ST-04.duplicates_eliminated: CN-12/CN-15 (CN implementations); TR-17 TSMOM (time-series form); RU-16 (MOEX replication).

ST-05.name: Value Factor (HML) & Value-Momentum Combination
ST-05.alt_names: 价值因子与价值动量组合 · Фактор стоимости
ST-05.origin: Fama & French 1992/1993; Asness, Moskowitz & Pedersen 'Value and Momentum Everywhere', JF 2013.
ST-05.core_idea: Long cheap (book/price, earnings/price) short expensive within industries; Asness et al. showed value and momentum are negatively correlated across every asset class, making their 50/50 combination the classic diversification machine. The CN twist is that value worked better than momentum historically on A-shares, driving CN-26's valuation-band popularity.
ST-05.rules: Rank by composite value metrics; long cheap decile (optionally short rich); rebalance annually/quarterly; combine with momentum 50/50.
ST-05.key_parameters: B/M or E/B ranks; industry-neutral form; rebalance 1-12 months.
ST-05.duplicates_eliminated: CN-26 (valuation timing); ST-09 quality-value hybrids; global smart-beta products.

ST-06.name: FX Carry Trade
ST-06.origin: Documented since the 1990s (BIS literature); Koijen, Moskowitz, Pedersen & Vrugt 'Carry', JFE 2018 formalized it everywhere.
ST-06.core_idea: Borrow low-yield currencies to buy high-yield ones, harvesting the forward-premium mispricing; returns are negatively skewed — years of grinding gains punctuated by violent unwinds. Systematic forms diversify across G10 pairs and add vol/regime filters. Carry also appears inside commodities and equities (roll yield, ST-16), making it the second universal factor.
ST-06.rules: Rank G10 by interest differential; long top, short bottom, vol-targeted; crash filter (momentum/vol gates) optional.
ST-06.duplicates_eliminated: CR-01 crypto funding carry (the perp analog); ST-16 commodity carry.

ST-07.name: Low-Volatility Anomaly
ST-07.alt_names: 低波动异象 · Аномалия низкой волатильности
ST-07.origin: Baker, Bradley & Wurgler, 'Benchmarks as Limits to Arbitrage', JFQA 2011 (building on Ang et al. 2006).
ST-07.core_idea: Low-beta/low-volatility stocks deliver higher risk-adjusted returns than the market — attributed to leverage constraints and benchmark-chasing incentives. Systematic forms long the lowest-vol quintile (optionally hedged), or tilt portfolios toward min-variance constructions. The anomaly is institutional-proof because it cannot be levered easily by benchmarked managers.
ST-07.rules: Rank by trailing 12-month vol; long bottom quintile; rebalance monthly/quarterly; optionally short the high-vol tail.
ST-07.key_parameters: Vol window 1-3 years; quintiles; quality screens to avoid value traps.
ST-07.duplicates_eliminated: ST-08 BAB (leverage-neutrality framing); min-variance portfolios; RU-16 replication.

ST-08.name: Betting Against Beta (BAB)
ST-08.alt_names: 贝塔对冲因子 · Betting Against Beta
ST-08.origin: Andrea Frazzini & Lasse Pedersen, 'Betting Against Beta', JFE 2014 (AQR).
ST-08.core_idea: Lever the low-beta half of stocks to beta-1, short the levered high-beta half to beta-1 — a market-neutral bet that high-beta assets underperform risk-adjusted. The construction isolates the anomaly that low-vol research described, with funding costs made explicit. It became the institutional vehicle for the constraint-based explanation of the low-vol puzzle.
ST-08.rules: Compute betas; construct two beta-1 portfolios; long-levered-low-beta minus short-levered-high-beta; rebalance with borrow-cost awareness.
ST-08.key_parameters: Beta window 1-5 years; leverage via futures/financing; quarterly rebalance.
ST-08.duplicates_eliminated: ST-07 (the unlevered view); global smart-beta funds.

ST-09.name: Quality / Profitability Factor (QMJ)
ST-09.origin: Robert Novy-Marx, 'The Other Side of Value: The Gross Profitability Premium', JFE 2013; Asness-Frazzini-Pedersen QMJ.
ST-09.core_idea: Profitable firms (gross profit/assets) outperform regardless of valuation; QMJ blends profitability, growth, and safety into the institutional quality factor. It anchors the quality-minus-junk framing used across CN 券商 factor reports and global fund marketing alike. As a system: long quality decile, optionally short junk, or use quality as a screen over other strategies.
ST-09.rules: Rank by gross profitability (and growth/safety in QMJ); long top decile; annual rebalance; combine with value for the classic quality-value pairing.
ST-09.key_parameters: GP/A primary; industry neutralization; rebalance 1-4 quarters.
ST-09.duplicates_eliminated: ST-05 (value pairing); Piotroski F-Score screens (cousin); CN-15 factor suite.

ST-10.name: WorldQuant 101 Formulaic Alphas
ST-10.origin: Zura Kakushadze, '101 Formulaic Alphas', arXiv:1601.00991 (2015); SSRN 2701346.
ST-10.core_idea: One hundred one explicit alpha formulas (ranks, time-series operators, price-volume constructs) that are simultaneously specification and code — published precisely to seed the crowd. The archive became the de-facto syllabus for CN quant education (DolphinDB implementations, WorldQuant BRAIN platform community) and the template for expression-based alpha mining. Individual alphas are weak; the corpus teaches construction grammar.
ST-10.rules: Example Alpha#1: rank(Ts_ArgMax(signedPower(returns < 0 ? stddev(returns,20) : close, 2), 5)) - 0.5 — long when the recent max of the conditional quantity happened early (positive alpha proxy).
ST-10.key_parameters: Per-alpha windows (5-20 days); cross-sectional rank requires a universe screener — single-symbol Pine proxies are documented as approximations.
ST-10.duplicates_eliminated: CN-15 (the CN platform implementations); BRAIN community alphas; DolphinDB 101-alpha ports.
ST-10.pine_code:
//@version=5
indicator("WorldQuant Alpha #1 (single-symbol proxy)", overlay=false)
ret = ta.roc(close, 1) / 100
sd = ta.stdev(ret, 20)
src = ret < 0 ? sd : close
// Ts_ArgMax over 5 bars of src^2: highestbars returns negative offset
argIdx = ta.highestbars(math.pow(src, 2), 5)
rankProxy = -argIdx / 5.0
alpha = rankProxy - 0.5
plot(alpha, "Alpha #1 proxy", color=alpha > 0 ? color.teal : color.red)
hline(0)

ST-11.name: The Factor Zoo & Multiple-Testing Corrections
ST-11.alt_names: 因子动物园与多重检验校正 · Факторный зоопарк
ST-11.origin: Harvey, Liu & Zhu, '...and the Cross-Section of Expected Returns', RFS 2016 (316 published factors); Green, Hand & Zhang 2017 (103 characteristics).
ST-11.core_idea: Hundreds of published return-predictors are catalogued, but multiple testing means a t-stat of 2.0 is meaningless at this scale — Harvey et al. recommend 3.0+ hurdles and document that most post-publication alpha decays. The 'factor' is thus itself a meta-strategy: demand higher bars, weight economic rationale, and expect decay. Every serious factor effort (CN-15, RU-16, BRAIN) now cites this work as hygiene.
ST-11.rules: Screen candidate factors by t > 3.0, out-of-sample persistence, and economic mechanism; monitor post-publication decay; penalize correlated duplicates.

ST-12.name: COT Positioning Strategies
ST-12.alt_names: CFTC持仓报告策略 · Стратегии по COT
ST-12.origin: CFTC Commitments of Traders reports (1962+ public data); Stephen Briese's commercialization (1990s); academic tests mixed.
ST-12.core_idea: Weekly positioning of commercials vs large specs encodes hedger conviction: extremes in speculator net-long (percentile-based) historically precede corrective phases in commodities. Systems fade positioning extremes or use them as filters for trend entries. Signal quality is regime-dependent and slow — it is a context factor more than a timing system.
ST-12.rules: Compute net-position percentiles (26-week window); fade spec extremes > 90th/< 10th percentile with trend confirmation.
ST-12.key_parameters: Percentile windows; report lag handling (Tuesday data, Friday release).
ST-12.duplicates_eliminated: Positioning analytics vendors; RU «отчёты COT» study groups; crypto COT-era analogs (BTC futures).

ST-13.name: Dispersion Trading (Index vs Constituents)
ST-13.core_idea: Index implied volatility systematically exceeds the average of constituent vols (correlation premium); short index options and long a basket of constituent options harvests the premium when realized correlation disappoints. It is correlation trading — the payout depends on realized vs implied correlation, not direction. Executable via variance swaps in modern markets.
ST-13.rules: Short index straddles/variants; long constituent straddles in vol-weighted amounts; delta-hedge; unwind at correlation normalization.
ST-13.key_parameters: Basket size 20-50 names; correlation window 60-250 days; vega neutrality.
ST-13.duplicates_eliminated: VRP (ST-14) at index level; dispersion desks' literature.

ST-14.name: Volatility Risk Premium Harvesting
ST-14.alt_names: 波动率风险溢价收割 · Сбор премии за волатильность
ST-14.origin: Documented across 1990s-2000s academic literature (Carr & Wu 2009 formalization); VIX-futures products industrialized it.
ST-14.core_idea: Implied vol systematically exceeds subsequent realized vol — sellers of insurance collect the premium; systematic short-vol (short VIX futures, put-selling with hedges) harvests it while carrying crash exposure. The February 2018 'Volmageddon' demonstrated the tail: levered short-vol ETPs died in a day. Modern implementations size by VRP estimate and cap leverage structurally.
ST-14.rules: Estimate VRP = implied - realized forecast; short vol when VRP > threshold with defined-risk structures; de-risk before events and after vol spikes.
ST-14.key_parameters: VRP estimate windows; defined-risk structures only; leverage caps.

ST-15.name: Gamma Scalping (Long-Gamma Rebalancing)
ST-15.origin: Options-desk canon (1980s+); formalized in dynamic-hedging literature (Taleb 1997).
ST-15.core_idea: Own options and delta-hedge continuously: each rebalance sells high/buys low, converting realized volatility into P&L at the cost of theta; profitable exactly when realized vol exceeds implied. It is the long side of ST-14 and the mechanism through which dealer hedging propagates volatility (the 2018/2024 vol events). Not Pine-implementable (needs options chain), so logic-only.
ST-15.rules: Long straddle/strangle; hedge delta to neutral at threshold crossings; monitor gamma-P&L vs theta bleed.
ST-15.key_parameters: Hedge threshold 0.1-0.2 delta; expiry choice by expected event calendar; position vega budget.
ST-15.duplicates_eliminated: ST-14 (the short side); dealer-flow research notes.

ST-16.name: Commodity Roll Yield / Contango Harvest
ST-16.origin: Gorton & Rouwenhorst, 'Facts and Fantasies about Commodity Futures', JF 2006; ETF-era lessons (2006-2015).
ST-16.core_idea: Futures curve shape (contango/backwardation) systematically transfers wealth between contract holders; long-in-backwardation/short-in-contango baskets harvest roll yield as a systematic return stream independent of spot direction. The 2000s commodity-ETF era's UIPath-style losses in contango (UNG) are the cautionary archive. It is carry (ST-06) in commodity form.
ST-16.rules: Rank commodity futures by roll yield (near-far spread annualized); long the most backwardated, short the most contangoed; roll monthly.
ST-16.key_parameters: Roll yield window; basket diversification 10+ commodities; contract liquidity filter.
ST-16.duplicates_eliminated: ST-06 carry; RU-06 synthetic bonds (financing-rate analog); CN-25 basis arb.

ST-17.name: Risk Parity & Volatility Targeting
ST-17.alt_names: 风险平价与波动率目标 · Паритет риска
ST-17.origin: Bridgewater's All Weather (1990s, Ray Dalio); Qian (2005) formalization; academic treatment 2010s.
ST-17.core_idea: Allocate so each asset class contributes equal risk rather than equal capital, leveraging the low-vol assets (bonds) to match equity risk; volatility targeting then scales total exposure inversely to realized vol. The 2022 bond-equity joint selloff exposed the regime-dependence of the correlations underneath. It is portfolio construction rather than signal — but it is the standard shell for factor portfolios.
ST-17.rules: Estimate covariance; solve equal-risk-contribution weights; leverage to target vol; rebalance quarterly or on drift.
ST-17.key_parameters: Target vol 8-12%; lookback 1-3 years; leverage/financing costs.
ST-17.duplicates_eliminated: ST-07/08 (risk-based tilts); GR-07 rebalancing (the retail cousin).

ST-18.name: Commodity Seasonality
ST-18.alt_names: 商品季节性策略 · Сезонность сырья
ST-18.origin: Decades of CTA practice; academic seasoning via seasonality papers (2000s-2010s).
ST-18.core_idea: Physical cycles (planting/harvest, heating season, OPEC logistics) create repeatable monthly drift patterns per commodity — e.g., heating oil strength into winter, gasoline into driving season. Systems long the statistically favorable months per contract with position sizing by pattern stability. The edges are small but persist because the physical driver persists.
ST-18.rules: Compute per-contract monthly return history; long months with stable positive historical drift; size by consistency score.
ST-18.key_parameters: History 15-30 years; consistency thresholds; roll handling.
ST-18.duplicates_eliminated: SE-05/06 (equity seasonality); RU grain-market seasonal notes; CN 农产品季节性 studies.

CR-01.name: Funding-Rate Arbitrage (Delta-Neutral Carry)
CR-01.alt_names: 资金费率套利 · Арбитраж фандинга
CR-01.origin: Perpetual futures funding design (BitMEX, 2016); exchange research notes and CN/RU crypto-bot communities (2019+).
CR-01.core_idea: Perps pay funding to anchor to spot: longs pay shorts when funding is positive. Holding spot long plus perp short harvests the funding while staying delta-neutral — the dominant structural carry of the 2020-2024 cycles, with double-digit annualized rates at bull peaks. Risk is funding flip, margin spirals, and exchange credit; executions exist as exchange-native 'funding arb' bots on CN and RU-facing venues alike.
CR-01.rules: Buy spot, short equal perp notional; collect funding while positive; close when funding turns negative after costs; ladder across venues.
CR-01.key_parameters: Funding threshold > 2 x fees per period; margin buffer 3-5x; venue diversification.
CR-01.duplicates_eliminated: ST-06 carry (the general form); CR-02 (dated-futures version).

CR-02.name: Cash-and-Carry / Futures Basis Trade
CR-02.origin: Classical arbitrage (RU-06's ancestor) reborn on CME/derivatives bases (2017+); documented in every post-2020 crypto research note.
CR-02.core_idea: When quarterly futures trade at a premium to spot (bull markets routinely 10-30% annualized), short the future, long spot, and hold to convergence — the premium is the return. It is the oldest arb in finance on the newest market, and its 2020-2021 magnitudes made it a flagship institutional crypto product. Same risk profile as CR-01 with dated convergence instead of indefinite funding.
CR-02.rules: Long spot / short dated future when annualized basis > threshold; hold to expiry or unwind at normalization; roll if the term structure stays steep.
CR-02.key_parameters: Basis threshold 8-15% annualized; margin buffer; expiry calendar.
CR-02.duplicates_eliminated: CR-01 (perp version); ST-16 (commodity roll analog); CN-25 (CN index-futures version).

CR-03.name: Liquidation-Cascade Fade
CR-03.alt_names: 爆仓瀑布反打 · Фейд каскада ликвидаций
CR-03.origin: Exchange data transparency (2019+); CN/RU crypto-Twitter communities; quantified by crypto research blogs.
CR-03.core_idea: Cascading liquidations drive price far past fair value within minutes — wicks of hundreds of dollars on BTC — because forced market orders exhaust the book; fading the cascade once liquidation flow exhausts (wick reversal, OI flush) targets the snap-back. Entry discipline is everything: only after OI/liquidation measures peak, never during. It is Wyckoff spring logic on an exchange-enforced timescale.
CR-03.rules: Detect abnormal wick + liquidation-volume spike + OI drop; enter reversal on the first reclaim bar; tight stop beyond wick; quick target at pre-cascade level.
CR-03.key_parameters: Wick > 2-3 ATR; liquidation percentile > 99th; holding minutes-to-hours.
CR-03.duplicates_eliminated: PA-01 spring (mechanism); VO-09 delta flush (informational cousin).

CR-04.name: Open-Interest Regime Model (OI + Price Matrix)
CR-04.alt_names: 持仓量状态模型 · Режимная модель OI
CR-04.origin: Derivatives-data platforms (Coinglass-era); CN/RU crypto communities' regime dashboards.
CR-04.core_idea: The OI x price quadrant classifies market state: OI up + price up = new longs (trend fuel), OI up + price down = new shorts, OI down + move = deleveraging (weak move), OI flat = range. Systems trade with new-position trends and fade deleveraging moves. It is the crypto analog of volume confirmation (VO family) built on a cleaner dataset.
CR-04.rules: Classify each bar into the OI-price quadrant; trade continuation in OI-building moves; fade post-flush moves as OI rebuilds.
CR-04.key_parameters: OI change thresholds vs ATR; quadrant persistence; funding context.
CR-04.duplicates_eliminated: VO-12 volume-confirmed breakout (tradfi analog); CR-03 (event special case).

CR-05.name: On-Chain Whale & Flow Following
CR-05.alt_names: 链上巨鲸跟踪 · Следование за китами
CR-05.origin: On-chain analytics platforms (Glassnode, Nansen era, 2019+); CN/RU crypto research communities.
CR-05.core_idea: Blockchain transparency exposes large-wallet behavior: exchange inflows (sell pressure), outflows (accumulation), stablecoin minting (dry powder), and smart-money wallet mimicry. Systems convert flow signals into regime gates or entry triggers — e.g., exchange net-outflow streaks precede supply squeezes. Data quality and interpretation lag are the binding caveats; attribution of wallets is probabilistic.
CR-05.rules: Track net exchange flows and whale-wallet cohorts; accumulate on outflow streaks + price basing; de-risk on inflow spikes with price strength.
CR-05.key_parameters: Flow thresholds vs circulating supply; cohort definitions; confirmation lag 1-7 days.
CR-05.duplicates_eliminated: CN-07/08 (flow-copy logic in tradfi clothes); VO order-flow family.

CR-06.name: BTC Dominance / Altcoin Rotation
CR-06.alt_names: BTC占比与山寨轮动 · Ротация BTC-альты
CR-06.origin: Crypto cycle literature (2017/2021 cycles); CN/RU altcoin communities.
CR-06.core_idea: Capital rotates through the crypto stack in cycles: BTC leads, then large alts, then speculative small caps, visible in BTC dominance charts; rotation systems shift weights along the dominance cycle and de-risk at blow-off signs. The edge is cycle timing, and its failure mode is staying late in the speculation phase. Implementations range from manual dashboards to automated dominance-momentum switches.
CR-06.rules: Track BTC dominance momentum; rotate BTC -> large alts -> small caps as dominance falls; reverse or go stable as dominance turns up sharply.
CR-06.key_parameters: Dominance windows 30-90 days; rotation thresholds; blow-off detection (funding, volume).
CR-06.duplicates_eliminated: CN-11 cap rotation (tradfi analog); TR-17 momentum machinery.

CR-07.name: Crypto Volatility Breakout (Donchian + Funding Filter)
CR-07.origin: Adaptation of TR-01/02 to 24/7 crypto (2017+ bot era); CN grid-vs-trend debates popularized the filter set.
CR-07.core_idea: Crypto trends hard; Donchian/ATR breakouts with a funding-regime filter (only long when funding is not extremely positive, avoiding crowded longs) capture major moves while avoiding the worst blow-off entries. Sizing is vol-normalized with wide stops because daily ATR can exceed 5-10%. It is the crypto workhorse trend shell.
CR-07.rules: Long on N-day high break when funding below crowd threshold; stop k x ATR; trail on opposite N/2-day low; short mirrored with funding context flipped.
CR-07.key_parameters: N 20-55; funding cap (e.g., < 0.05%/8h for longs); stop 2-4 ATR.
CR-07.duplicates_eliminated: TR-01/TR-02 (parents); SE-09 (session overlays); RU/CN crypto-bot presets.

CR-08.name: Triangular Arbitrage
CR-08.origin: FX desk-era technique; cryptoized 2017+ (high-frequency bots; CN/RU arbitrage communities).
CR-08.core_idea: Exploit inconsistencies across three-leg cycles (BTC/USDT, ETH/USDT, ETH/BTC) where implied cross rates diverge beyond fees; profits are tick-scale and vanish with latency, making this an HFT-adjacent game of infrastructure rather than strategy. Documented because it is the canonical answer to 'can retail arb crypto?' — usually no, at speed.
CR-08.rules: Monitor implied cross vs quoted; execute all three legs atomically when edge > 3x fees; cancel on leg failure.
CR-08.key_parameters: Edge threshold; execution latency < 50 ms realistically; fee tier optimization.

CR-09.name: DeFi Concentrated Liquidity Market-Making
CR-09.alt_names: DeFi做市策略 · DeFi ММ (Uniswap v3)
CR-09.origin: Uniswap v3 whitepaper (2021); DeFi research and CN/RU DeFi communities.
CR-09.core_idea: Concentrated-liquidity positions earn fees proportional to capital efficiency within a chosen range; the strategy is choosing ranges around expected mean-reversion zones, managing inventory drift (impermanent loss is rebalancing), and compounding fees. It is market-making with a public, non-custodial venue — and its risk profile (inventory + range exit) is classic MM risk in new clothes.
CR-09.rules: Provide liquidity in a range around fair value; re-center on drift; widen ranges in high-vol regimes; compound fees.
CR-09.key_parameters: Range width vs ATR; rebalance drift threshold; fee tier selection; gas budget.
CR-09.duplicates_eliminated: GR-01 grid (the AMM is a grid at heart); VO order-flow family (inventory logic).

CR-10.name: MEV Extraction (Sandwich / Backrun) — Documented, Not Endorsed
CR-10.origin: Flash Boys 2.0 paper (Daian et al., 2019); MEV research (Flashbots era).
CR-10.core_idea: Public mempools let bots see pending swaps and extract value by front/back-running them, an estimated billion-dollar category; the strategy is pure latency-plus-auction economics, and the countermeasure evolution (private RPCs, batch auctions, MEV-boost) is one of the great market-structure stories of the decade. Listed for completeness with the explicit note that it is adversarial extraction, increasingly disintermediated by protocol design.
CR-10.rules: Detection of profitable pending transactions; bundle bidding via MEV infrastructure; economics capped by priority-auction competition.
CR-10.key_parameters: Bid competitiveness; bundle profitability floor; infra costs.

CR-11.name: Cross-Exchange Latency Arbitrage
CR-11.alt_names: 跨所延迟套利 · Межбиржевой арбитраж
CR-11.origin: 2017+ crypto fragmentation era; CN (pre-ban) and RU arbitrage communities extensively documented it.
CR-11.core_idea: Price discovery leads on the deepest venue (Binance/CME); lagging venues drift a few basis points behind, and fast bots synchronize by buying the lag and hedging the lead. Withdrawal/transfer risk and fee tiers decide viability; the modern edge is mostly dead at retail latency. It completes the arbitrage subset of this family and marks the boundary where strategy ends and infrastructure begins.
CR-11.rules: Lead venue defines fair price; trade laggards when divergence > 2 x costs; hedge or transfer inventory; risk = transfer/counterparty.
CR-11.key_parameters: Divergence threshold; inventory rebalancing cadence; venue credit risk.
CR-11.duplicates_eliminated: CR-08 (same-latency family); CN-era '搬砖' (brick-moving) practice — the CN name for exactly this trade.

ML-01.name: Gradient-Boosted Factor Models (XGBoost/LightGBM Alpha)
ML-01.alt_names: 机器学习多因子选股 · XGBoost/LightGBM альфа
ML-01.origin: 华泰证券金工 '人工智能选股' series (2017+); JoinQuant/BigQuant template canon; Kaggle-era ubiquity.
ML-01.core_idea: Feed hundreds of factors into gradient-boosted trees to predict next-month relative returns, with purged walk-forward validation and industry neutralization; CN broker research published extensive public backtests making this the most-documented ML workflow in Chinese. Trees handle nonlinear factor interactions and missing data gracefully, which is why they beat linear IC-weighting in CN studies — when validation is honest.
ML-01.rules: Feature matrix = factor panel; label = forward returns; train with purged k-fold; trade top-decile predictions monthly; monitor feature importance drift.
ML-01.key_parameters: Depth 3-6; learning rate 0.05-0.1; purge gap = label horizon; retrain quarterly.
ML-01.duplicates_eliminated: CN-15 (the linear factor parent); ST-10 (expression-alphas as features); JoinQuant ML templates.

ML-02.name: LSTM / Sequence Models for Direction
ML-02.alt_names: 长短期记忆网络方向预测 · LSTM-прогноз
ML-02.origin: Academic literature surge 2017-2020 (Fischer & Krauss LSTM on DAX, 2018, the canonical citation).
ML-02.core_idea: Sequence models ingest windows of returns/volumes and classify next-period direction; the canonical result shows in-sample promise and fast post-publication decay as the edge is regime-specific. Honest deployments treat the model as one ensemble vote with strict walk-forward and transaction-cost stress, not an oracle. The family's lesson is statistical: sequence overfitting is spectacular and easy.
ML-02.rules: Window 30-60 bars of normalized features; binary/ternary direction labels; purged walk-forward; ensemble with simpler signals; deploy at reduced size.
ML-02.key_parameters: Hidden 32-128; dropout 0.2-0.5; retrain cadence; cost-adjusted threshold tuning.

ML-03.name: Reinforcement Learning Portfolios (FinRL lineage)
ML-03.alt_names: 强化学习组合管理 · RL-портфели
ML-03.origin: FinRL (AI4Finance, 2020+) and the deep-RL trading literature (2018+).
ML-03.core_idea: An agent learns allocation/sizing policies against simulated environments with transaction costs, optimizing risk-adjusted objectives rather than supervised labels. Research results are mixed and environment design dominates outcomes: realistic fills, costs, and regime shifts decide whether learned policies generalize. Its lasting contribution is the environment library that forces honest simulation.
ML-03.rules: Define state (prices/positions), action space (weights), reward (Sharpe or CVaR-adjusted); train on regime-diverse data; paper-trade learned policies before capital.
ML-03.key_parameters: PPO/SAC agents; cost model fidelity; out-of-distribution guards.

ML-04.name: HMM Regime Switching
ML-04.alt_names: 隐马尔可夫状态切换 · HMM-режимы
ML-04.core_idea: A hidden Markov model fits latent market states (bull/bear/chop) from return-volatility emissions; regime probabilities gate other strategies — enabling trend systems only in trending states, reversion in chop. It is the statistical formalization of 'the market changes character', and its biggest value is honest uncertainty: low-confidence regimes trigger de-risking rather than guessing.
ML-04.rules: Fit 2-4 state HMM on returns/vol; gate strategy family by state probability > threshold; de-risk in transition uncertainty.
ML-04.key_parameters: States 2-4; emissions gaussian/t; retrain monthly; smoothing lag.
ML-04.duplicates_eliminated: SE-08 (calendar regimes); TR-07 ADX gates (the indicator-flavored ancestor).

ML-05.name: NLP Sentiment & News Trading
ML-05.origin: FinBERT lineage (2019+); CN snownlp-era sentiment factors; RU SMM-sentiment studies.
ML-05.core_idea: Score news/social text with domain-tuned language models and trade the sentiment-return relationship: announcement-day drift after strong sentiment, headline-momentum on novel information. Latency and event deduplication decide viability — much of the exploitable signal lives in the first seconds, which retail pipelines cannot reach; the slower tail (analyst reports, regulatory filings) is more accessible.
ML-05.rules: Ingest/score text; deduplicate events; trade drift windows (hours-days) on sentiment extremes with trend/liquidity gates.
ML-05.key_parameters: Model domain-tuning; decay half-life of signal; event-window definitions.
ML-05.duplicates_eliminated: CN-05 (sentiment regime cousin); ST-04 (momentum on information flow).

ML-06.name: Genetic Algorithms & Parameter Search
ML-06.alt_names: 遗传算法参数寻优 · Генетическая оптимизация
ML-06.origin: 1990s EA-era practice (MT4 strategy tester 'genetic mode'); Adaptrade-style tools; RU/CN optimizer culture.
ML-06.core_idea: Evolutionary search over parameter spaces maximizes backtest fitness — powerful, and the single fastest way to overfit if fitness is raw P&L on one sample. Disciplined forms optimize on rolling windows with walk-forward scoring, penalty for parameter cliffs, and ensemble-over-parameters deployment. Documented as methodology rather than a strategy per se.
ML-06.rules: Encode parameters; evolve on training windows; score out-of-sample; select plateau regions (robust sets) not peaks; ensemble survivors.
ML-06.key_parameters: Population/generations modest; fitness = walk-forward Sharpe with cost stress; plateau selection.
ML-06.duplicates_eliminated: ML-07 (the evaluation discipline); RU «генетический оптимизатор» MT4 heritage.

ML-07.name: Walk-Forward, Deflated Sharpe & Overfitting Control
ML-07.alt_names: 滚动前推与紧缩夏普 · Контроль переобучения
ML-07.origin: Robert Pardo (walk-forward, 1992); Bailey & López de Prado deflated Sharpe / probability of backtest overfitting (2014-2017).
ML-07.core_idea: The meta-strategy of the whole glossary: validate by rolling re-optimization out-of-sample, correct Sharpe for the number of trials attempted, and estimate the probability that the best-of-N backtest is luck. These tools — not any single entry signal — separate the surviving quant funds from the graveyard. Every entry above should be run through this discipline before capital.
ML-07.rules: Walk-forward with anchored/rolling windows; count all trials for deflated Sharpe; require PBO < threshold; prefer parameter plateaus.
ML-07.key_parameters: Window ratios (train 4x test typical); trials ledger; Sharpe hurdle adjusted by N.
ML-07.duplicates_eliminated: ML-06 (the search it disciplines); postcheck for every CN/RU platform strategy.

RX-01.name: Fixed Fractional / Percent-Risk Sizing
RX-01.alt_names: 固定比例风险仓位 · Фикс-фракционное позиционирование
RX-01.origin: Ralph Vince, Portfolio Management Formulas (1990); universal practice since.
RX-01.core_idea: Size every trade so that the stop distance equals a fixed fraction of equity (0.5-2%): losses scale down in drawdowns and up in recoveries, giving geometric growth bounded by the risk fraction. It is the professional default and the direct generalization of the Turtle unit. The subtleties are volatility-of-volatility and gap risk beyond the stop.
RX-01.rules: Quantity = (equity x risk%) / (entry - stop); recompute per trade; cap gaps with position limits.
RX-01.duplicates_eliminated: TR-02 Turtle units (the volatility-normalized ancestor); every platform's default sizing.

RX-02.name: Kelly & Half-Kelly Criterion
RX-02.alt_names: 凯利公式与半凯利 · Критерий Келли
RX-02.origin: John Kelly, Bell System Technical Journal 1956; Thorp's 1960s-70s market applications.
RX-02.core_idea: Kelly sizing f* = p - q/b maximizes long-run logarithmic growth; full Kelly is uninvestable in practice (variance brutal, edge estimates wrong), so practitioners use half or quarter Kelly. The formula's real lesson is that sizing and edge are inseparable — overbetting turns any positive-expectancy system into ruin. Implemented here as a Pine helper for educational sizing.
RX-02.rules: Estimate win rate and win/loss ratio; size fraction = k x Kelly with k = 0.25-0.5; re-estimate on rolling trade history.
RX-02.key_parameters: Rolling sample 30-100 trades; k fraction; caps by volatility budget.
RX-02.duplicates_eliminated: RX-01 (the practical constrained form); prop-firm sizing policies.
RX-02.pine_code:
//@version=5
indicator("Kelly Sizing Helper", overlay=false)
winRate = input.float(55.0, "Win rate %")
avgWin  = input.float(1.8, "Average win (R)")
avgLoss = input.float(1.0, "Average loss (R)")
kelly(p, b) => p - (1 - p) / b
f = kelly(winRate / 100, avgWin / avgLoss)
plot(f * 100, "Kelly %", color=f > 0 ? color.teal : color.red)
hline(0)

RX-03.name: Volatility-Targeted Sizing (ATR Units)
RX-03.alt_names: 波动率目标仓位 · Волатильно-таргетированный размер
RX-03.origin: Turtle 'N' doctrine (TR-02); CTA standard practice; risk-parity (ST-17) single-asset form.
RX-03.core_idea: Scale positions inversely to recent volatility so each trade contributes equal risk regardless of the instrument's storminess — the quiet insight that lets one system trade rebar, crude, and equities coherently. Combined with a portfolio vol target it is the standard CTA architecture. Its failure mode is the vol spike that hits after the signal but before the resize.
RX-03.rules: Position = target risk / ATR; portfolio vol target scales total exposure; adjust at vol-shift thresholds, not every bar.
RX-03.key_parameters: ATR window 14-20; per-trade risk 0.5-1%; portfolio target 10-15% annualized.

RX-04.name: Portfolio Heat & Correlation Limits
RX-04.alt_names: 组合热度与相关性限制 · Портфельный «нагрев»
RX-04.origin: Prop/CTA risk management canon (1990s+); documented in CTA risk literature.
RX-04.core_idea: Heat = total open risk (sum of each position's stop-distance loss) as a fraction of equity; capping heat (e.g., 6%) and per-correlation-cluster heat (e.g., 3%) is what prevents five 'good trades' in the same factor from becoming one giant trade. Cluster-aware limits require mapping positions to common factors — the discipline that separates professionals from account blowups.
RX-04.rules: Sum open risk; block new entries above heat caps; cluster positions by factor/correlation and cap per cluster.
RX-04.key_parameters: Total heat 4-8%; cluster heat 2-3%; correlation threshold 0.6+.

RX-05.name: Breakeven Ratchet & Scale-Out Exits
RX-05.alt_names: 保本推进与分批止盈 · Безубыток и частичная фиксация
RX-05.origin: Universal trader practice; formalized in exit-engineering literature (LeBeau lineage).
RX-05.core_idea: Two exit upgrades that dominate expectancy: moving the stop to breakeven at a profit threshold (converting trades to free options at the cost of some win rate), and scaling out at fixed R multiples (banking base + letting a runner work). Their interaction with trend systems is the classic tension — ratchets cut winners early. Implemented as a reusable Pine exit shell.
RX-05.rules: At +kR, stop to entry; scale out fractions at 1R/2R/3R or by ATR bands; trail the remainder.
RX-05.key_parameters: k 0.8-1.5R; scale fractions 50/25/25; trail on remainder.
RX-05.duplicates_eliminated: TR-10 trailing stops (the pure trail); GR-03 pyramids' exit side.
RX-05.pine_code:
//@version=5
strategy("Breakeven Ratchet Exit Shell", overlay=true)
rMult  = input.float(1.0, "BE at (R)")
atrMult = input.float(2.0, "Initial stop ATR")
atr = ta.atr(14)
if strategy.position_size == 0
strategy.entry("L", strategy.long)
var float stopPx = na
if strategy.position_size > 0
if na(stopPx)
stopPx := strategy.position_avg_price - atrMult * atr
gainR = (high - strategy.position_avg_price) / (atrMult * atr)
if gainR >= rMult
stopPx := math.max(stopPx, strategy.position_avg_price)
strategy.exit("LX", from_entry="L", stop=stopPx)
if strategy.position_size == 0
stopPx := na

RX-06.name: Time Stops & Opportunity-Cost Exits
RX-06.origin: Prop-desk doctrine ('dead money is negative money'); quantified in TASC-era exit studies.
RX-06.core_idea: If a trade has not moved favorably within N bars, its premise is stale: exit and recycle capital into live setups. Backtests consistently show time stops improve capital efficiency even when they slightly reduce average win, because the opportunity cost of parked capital compounds. The parameter is regime-sensitive — swing trades need days, scalps need minutes.
RX-06.rules: Exit if unrealized P&L below a threshold after N bars (or if no new high/low within N bars); re-entry rules unchanged.
RX-06.key_parameters: N by style (3-10 bars intraday, 5-20 days swing); dead-money threshold.
RX-06.duplicates_eliminated: CN-02 board time-stop; BK-01 session-flat rule (time stop by clock).

RX-07.name: Execution Algorithms (TWAP / VWAP / POV) & Slippage Budgets
RX-07.alt_names: 算法交易与滑点预算 · Алго-исполнение
RX-07.origin: Institutional execution research (Bertsimas-Lo 1998; Almgren-Chriss 2000); retail access via broker APIs.
RX-07.core_idea: Large orders are strategies too: TWAP slices time, VWAP tracks volume curve, POV participates at a market-share rate — each trading off market impact against timing risk. The retail-relevant lesson is the slippage budget: every strategy entry in this glossary must reserve costs (spread + impact + fees) that often decide viability more than the signal itself. Quantifying them is the last mile between backtest and P&L.
RX-07.rules: Slice parent orders per the chosen curve; randomize child sizes; measure realized slippage vs benchmark; feed the measurement back into strategy viability.
RX-07.key_parameters: Participation 5-20%; impact model by ADV; cost ledger per strategy.
RX-07.duplicates_eliminated: VO-07/08 (VWAP as signal — same benchmark, different job); RU-13/CR-08 (latency-bound execution domains).
